WATCH THE REVIEW

excerpt:
If you love cute rock tunes with a dismal outlook on life, Veronica Falls might be the band for you. Their latest LP is simple, immediate, and catchy. I know it’s easy to get down on something that sounds so easy to execute, but the energy and moody aesthetic that surround this band are something worth admiring to me.

title: Das Racist- Relax
excerpt:
Das Racist’s Relax is a bit of a letdown for me. I just didn’t enjoy it as much as the tapes. There are plenty of tracks here where the guys are their usual, hilarious selves. WATCH THE REVIEW

excerpt:
Ah, the new Opeth record. Was I expecting to like this? No. Was I hoping I’d like this? Yes! A big, fat “yes,” actually.

I’ve never been an Opeth fan. Their melodic and almost overproduced take on death metal–and progressive metal, generally–just doesn’t have anything I look for in music.

Deftones make a lighter and more ethereal left turn with their latest album, much like they did with Saturday Night Wrist in 2006, but the end result is nowhere near as experimental or expansive, unfortunately. title: Unknown Mortal Orchestra- Self-Titled

Unknown Mortal Orchestra’s debut full-length surprised me in some places, but underwhelmed in others. I love how effortlessly these guys pull together a fun and bouncy salute to the world of 60s rock and pop. It sounds as fresh as it does retro.

Where this album really ended up losing me, though, was in the song structures, which repeat to the point where a lot of these songs sorta lose their flavor.

excerpt:

This record isn’t completely devoid of fun or flavor. The Johns’ usual buffet of strong melodies, catchy hooks, and esoteric lyrics is here. If anything on this album will keep longtime fans happy, it’s that.

I don’t think I was expecting the world of this album–especially since the last album didn’t give me the world. To put it simply, I guess I was expecting something different. To me, this album feels like a serious and well-recorded version of Psychic Chasms.

title: La Dispute- Wildlife

La Dispute’s Wildlife is a fantastic and rewarding gauntlet of emotional rock music. Even if post-hardcore isn’t in your comfort zone, this album is worth a shot.

excerpt:
On the Future Islands’ new album, they continue breeding the simple, bare, and dramatic style of synth pop that caught ears in 2010 on the group’s last album, In Evening Air.

title: Mastodon- The Hunter
excerpt:
On the Hunter, Mastodon’s sludgy take on progressive metal is sounding more accessible than ever.

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Jacaszek- Glimmer
excerpt:
Jacaszek’s latest release is an eerily beautiful blend of classical instrumentation, indescribable noises, and interesting edits. Oh, yeah, there’s some ambient influences in there, too.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Drake- Take Care
excerpt:
On Drake’s latest album, the Canadian rapper and singer embraces what makes him unique, and sounds great doing it. There is a noticeable hunk of filler on this LP, though.

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Pianos Become the Teeth- The Lack Long After
excerpt:
On Pianos Become the Teeth’s sophomore LP, the band sports all the qualities I look for in a screamo group. However, they stop short of separating themselves from many of the bands in this style.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Jonti- Sine & Moon
excerpt:
Download: Jonti- Sine & Moon

Last year, Austalia beat producer and multi-instrumentalist Jonti made his Stones Throw debut with the album Twirligig. Now, he’s following that release up with a free album, Sine & Moon. This .zip is a combo of trippy hip hop instrumentals, pretty interludes, and experimental psych pop. Very rich, very colorful.

title: The Shins- "Simple Song"
excerpt:
The Shins drop a track from its forthcoming album Port of Morrow, and I’m pretty surprised by the large and ambitious sounds the track shows off.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Nujabes- Spiritual State
excerpt:
Considering it’s a posthumous album, Nujabes’ Spiritual State has some pretty great tracks on it. Still, I think it’s best to leave this one to the fans.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Lamb of God- Resolution
excerpt:
Lamb of God’s sixth studio album is big on aggression, which is to be expected, but it doesn’t exactly bring enough ideas to the table to keep things interesting for me.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Leonard Cohen- Old Ideas
excerpt:
On his latest album, singer-songwriter presents exactly what this album’s title suggests. I just wish the instrumentation sounded better.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Moonface- With Siinai: Heartbreaking Bravery
excerpt:
While it is exciting for me to be hearing singer-songwriter Spencer Krug fronting a band once again on the latest album to come out of his Moonface project, this album, for many reasons, didn’t measure up to my expectations.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Dr. John- Locked Down
excerpt:
With Dan Auerbach of the Black Keys producing, the new Dr. John album sees the New Orleands R&B legend revitalized with a dark and rustic aesthetic.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: mewithoutYou- Ten Stories
excerpt:
With Ten Stories, mewithoutYou comes to a somewhat underwhelming middle-ground with the post-hardcore and folk influences that informed the band’s previous two records.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: B.o.B- Strange Clouds
excerpt:
On his sophomore release, B.o.B climbs further up the mainstream ladder by continuing to blend hip hop with some of the poppiest sounds imaginable. While a few singles in this style aren’t bad, B.o.B overdoes it a bit by making nearly every track shoot for some kind of pre-chewed, radio-friendly sound. The end result is an album that doesn’t feel all that personal or engaging. Rather, it’s pretty one-size-fits all.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Torche- Harmonicraft
excerpt:
Thought Torche’s stomping grounds are firmly rooted in loud rock and metal, the band’s latest album is so bright, catchy, and sweet, even the most biggest of metal cynics can get something out of it.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Neil Young & Crazy Horse- Americana
excerpt:
On Neil Young’s latest release with longtime band Crazy Horse, these guys bring together a collection of songs important to the history of American music, filtering them through a series of fast and loose folk rock jams.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: El-P- "The Full Retard"
excerpt:
Some hilarious visuals coming from El-P on this new music video for “the Full Retard,” which is a track from the New York rapper’s latest album, Cancer For Cure. It’s like a weird, coked-out scene from Fear and Loathing In Las Vegas, except the Dr. Gonzo to El-P’s Raoul Duke is a ratty-lookin’ squirrel puppet.


/via/

title: Best Coast- The Only Place
excerpt:
I’ve returned to Best Coast’s music almost out of a morbid curiosity just to find I’m even less in love with this album than I was the California rock and pop outfit’s debut.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Between the Buried and Me- The Parallax II: Future Sequence
excerpt:
On their sixth studio album, Between the Buried and Me creates its campiest album yet, blending their usual progressive tendencies with the overly theatrical antics of bands like Dream Theater.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Bloc Party- Four
excerpt:
Bloc Party returns after a self-imposed hiatus with a true blue rock album.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Recondite- On Acid

On his debut full-length, German music producer Recondite assembles a collection of beautiful, atmospheric experimentations on acid house music.



WATCH THE REVIEW

Roomful of Teeth is an intriguingly strange choral group whose debut, self-titled album adventurously expands what it means to make music in this genre.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Titus Andronicus- Local Business
excerpt:
On its third full-length, New Jersey’s Titus Andronicus goes a bit simpler, but still maintains the life-affirming energy that made past releases so good.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Pile- Dripping
excerpt:
On their third full-length release, Boston’s Pile connects the heavy hitting sounds of post-hardcore with the dramatic and melodic songwriting prowess of frontman Rick Maguire.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Shlohmo / Justin Timberlake / Factory Floor / Fidlar / Mystical Weapons / Ra Ra Riot / Chris Owens w/the Quickness
excerpt:
I mention and quickly review the latest releases and songs from the likes of Factory Floor, Shlohmo, Christopher Owens, Mystical Weapons, Ra Ra Riot, Low, Four Tet, and more!

excerpt:
Screamo outfit Circle Takes the Square are back with their first full length in about 8 years.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Milo - Things That Happen and Day / Things That Happen at Night
excerpt:
On his new set of EPs, Wisconsin rapper Rory Ferreira, a.k.a. Milo, changes his instrumental game, rapping over some pretty spacious, atmospheric beats. On top of that, he’s strengthened his usual barrage of obtuse personal musings; bringing their emotional potency higher than ever.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Flaming Lips - The Terror
excerpt:
On their latest full-length, The Flaming Lips bring vivid sounds and a strong aesthetic, but don’t offer the songs, execution, or variety to back it up.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Flaming Lips, Voivod, Nails, The Knife, Bleeding Rainbow, and more w/the Quickness
excerpt:
Yet again, a group of mentions and cursory reviews of things I didn’t get a chance to talk about this past week!

title: Deafheaven - "Dream House"
excerpt:
Atmospheric black metal outfit Deafheaven returns with the first single from their sophomore release, Sunbather.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Yeah Yeah Yeahs - Mosquito
excerpt:
Unfortunately, the latest Yeah Yeah Yeahs album is one of those instances when the album’s lead single seems to be the best track, dwarfing nearly every other song on the album with ambition, glitz, and great songwriting. The rest of the album is a bit spotty, in my opinion.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Kurt VIle - Wakin On A Pretty Daze
excerpt:
On his latest full-length, Philly singer-songwriter Kurt Vile shows more ambition through his approach to psychedelic folk with longer songs, detailed instrumentation, and sublime production.

title: Janelle Monáe - The Electric Lady
excerpt: With the Electric Lady, singer-songwriter and composer Janelle Monáe adds two more suites to her ongoing metropolis series. This time, she seems to embrace her classic influences in the worlds of R&B and soul closer than ever.

title: AlunaGeorge - Body Music
excerpt:
With some diverse production and memorable hooks, UK pop duo AlunaGeorge come through with a relatively solid debut album.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Boards of Canada - Tomorrow's Harvest
excerpt:
After about eight years of silence, Boards of Canada return with Tomorrow’s Harvest, which might be their saddest and most desolate record to date; directly emulating much of the progressive synth and soundtrack music that has always informed the duo’s style.

However, there are a slew of different factors keeping this record from sticking out in Ty’s ever-growing discography: production, songwriting, vocals. All of these things keep Fuzz from feeling like a truly distinct moment–even though Ty and Charlie are shooting for an entirely different style of rock on this record. title: White Suns - Totem

title: Sadsic - Self-Titled

title: Glasser - Interiors

While her music was obviously influenced, it was still really enjoyable. Interiors changes things in that regard, however. This time around, Cameron seems to be drowning in her love of one particular artist: Björk.

excerpt: This album is about death.

title: Power Trip - Nightmare Logic
excerpt: Power Trip’s second album for Southern Lord Records brings thrash metal back with a fucking vengeance.

title: Pallbearer - Heartless
excerpt: Little Rock doom outfit Pallbearer returns with more bite and an even greater prog influence on their third album Heartless, their most varied and epic effort yet.

title: Gas - Narkopop
excerpt: 17 years after his landmark album Pop, ambient music producer Wolfgang Voigt has finally given us the night to that album’s day… and I really wish he didn’t.

title: Forest Swords - Compassion
excerpt: On his sophomore album Compassion, Forest Swords’ unique style of dramatic, meditative, and primal ambient dub offers some much needed respite from the trend-chasing nature of modern electronic music.

title: Slowdive - Self-Titled
excerpt: Slowdive’s first album in over two decades finds the band’s once heavenly wall of sound turning anemic.

title: B.o.B - Ether
excerpt: B.o.B makes the corniest B.o.B album yet.

title: SZA - Ctrl
excerpt: SZA delivers a strong full-length debut that explores the emotional complexities of being the other woman.

title: Lil Yachty - Teenage Emotions
excerpt: Lil Yachty’s debut album is a horrific disappointment.

title: JAY-Z - 4:44
excerpt: Mr. Carter kills his ego and spills the beans on his most intimate album yet.

title: Haim - Something to Tell You
excerpt: The Haim sisters return with a front-loaded sophomore album.

title: Vic Mensa - The Autobiography
excerpt: Vic Mensa’s long-awaited debut album delivers its fair share of grand and thoughtful highs, but also some cringe-worthy lows.

title: Nine Inch Nails - Add Violence
excerpt: Nine Inch Nails follows up last year’s Not the Actual Events EP with a moodier and more atmospheric set of tracks, which I don’t find to be quite as well-written or exciting.

title: Dying Fetus - Wrong One to Fuck With
excerpt: Maryland trio Dying Fetus comes through with one of the best brutal death metal albums I’ve heard since their last album back in 2012.

title: Richard Dawson - Peasant
excerpt: Richard Dawson’s sprawling and rustic tunes bring back a sense of olde English folklore and mysticism that isn’t often heard in contemporary music.

title: Igorrr - Savage Sinusoid
excerpt: Despite faltering in its third act, Savage Sinusoid is so far Igorrr’s most palatable blend of breakcore, metal, and baroque sounds.

title: A$AP Mob - Cozy Tapes Vol. 2: Too Cozy
excerpt: It’s telling that one of the few highlights on Cozy Tapes Vol. 2 is a track with little to no A$AP Mob presence.

title: Queens of the Stone Age - Villains
excerpt: Mark Ronson’s flat production doesn’t do any favors for Villains, Queens of the Stone Age’s most mixed bag of tracks to date.

title: Brand New - Science Fiction
excerpt: Brand New returns with a chilling, despondent sound.

title: Alex Cameron - Forced Witness
excerpt: On his sophomore album, Sydney singer/songwriter Alex Cameron consistently delivers catchy hooks and hilarious lyrics while channeling a soft rock aesthetic.

title: Action Bronson - Blue Chips 7000
excerpt: Action Bronson continues to bring the humor, the flow, and the heart on Blue Chips 7000, but the album is pretty underdeveloped on the whole.

title: Foo Fighters - Concrete and Gold
excerpt: Post-grunge veterans Foo Fighters drop a raw but spotty album with Concrete and Gold.

title: Myrkur - Mareridt
excerpt: Myrkur’s sophomore album still leaves something to be desired on the songwriting front, but is nevertheless a much better-developed product than her debut.

title: Godspeed You! Black Emperor - "Luciferian Towers"
excerpt: “Luciferian Towers” is the first Godspeed album we didn’t need.

title: Rapsody - Laila's Wisdom
excerpt: Rapsody releases her most solid project to date with the smart, classy, and catchy Laila’s Wisdom.

title: Protomartyr - Relatives in Descent
excerpt: Loaded with poetic post-punk dirges, Protomartyr’s Relatives in Descent is the Detroit band’s most dynamic and well-written release yet.

title: Marilyn Manson - Heaven Upside Down
excerpt: Shock rock legend Marilyn Manson returns with his 10th album, Heaven Upside Down.

title: Wolves in the Throne Room - Thrice Woven
excerpt: Wolves in the Throne Room make a predictable return to their atmospheric black metal sound.

title: Rina Sawayama - RINA
excerpt: UK pop singer Rina Sawayama teams up with Clarence Clarity for the most vibrant, colorful, and instantly catchy pop EP of the year.

title: Weezer - Pacific Daydream
excerpt: Weezer indulge in millennial pop cliches on their most sugar-sweet album yet, Pacific Daydream.

title: Joji - "Will He"
excerpt: With his In Tongues EP on the way, Joji drops a melancholic new single.

title: Destroyer - ken
excerpt: Destroyer’s latest record is an awkward helping of new wave pastiche.

title: Taylor Swift - Reputation
excerpt: Reputation focuses more on the pop star narrative than it does actual pop songs.

title: Benjamin Clementine - I Tell a Fly
excerpt: British singer-songwriter Benjamin Clementine brings more bells and whistles on his sophomore album I Tell a Fly, but it’s unfortunately a case of more being less.

title: Sharon Jones & The Dap-Kings - Soul of a Woman
excerpt: Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings’ final record is a celebration of everything that made the soul revivalists great since their inception in the early ’00s.

title: Jaden Smith - SYRE
excerpt: Jaden Smith’s latest film is an auditory one, exploring the lyrical follies of a rich-kid-turned-mediocre-rapper in desperate need of perspective as he produces 70 minutes of egotistical propaganda in the hope it will launch his rap career.

title: Liars - TFCF
excerpt: Liars’ TFCF is one of the band’s most isolated, tedious, and disappointing releases yet.

title: Lauryn Hill - The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
excerpt: Lauryn Hill’s sole solo album is a masterful fusion of R&B, hip hop, and soul music.

title: N*E*R*D - NO_ONE EVER REALLY DIES
excerpt: N*E*R*D’s latest is a somewhat inconsistent return, but offers some of the freshest production of 2017.

title: GFOTY - GFOTYBUCKS
excerpt: With GFOTYBUCKS, PC Music’s GFOTY has created a disorienting collage of absurdly hedonistic electropop.

title: Jeff Rosenstock - Post-
excerpt: The New York songwriter’s latest work feels like a pale presentation of the anthemic punk style of his previous record, Worry.

title: Aphex Twin - Selected Ambient Works 85-92
excerpt: Richard D. James’ first full-length under the Aphex Twin name still stands as a landmark moment in contemporary electronic music.

title: Ween - Chocolate and Cheese
excerpt: Ween’s first professionally recorded studio album is an oddball rock classic.

title: Ty Segall - Freedom's Goblin
excerpt: Sometimes cumbersome but mostly exciting, Ty Segall’s latest album is his longest and most ambitious yet.

title: Kanye West - The Life of Pablo (Redux)
excerpt: Anthony makes a remarkably timely return to the final version of Kanye West’s experimental opus, The Life of Pablo.

title: CupcakKe - Ephorize
excerpt: Ephorize is cupcakKe’s most consistent and entertaining album yet.

title: Tribulation - Down Below
excerpt: Tribulation comes through with a pretty solid gothic metal album that you’ll want to light your candelabra to.

title: Rich Brian - Amen
excerpt: Rich Brian shows more personality than many of his contemporaries on his debut project, but his sound is a bit too one-note to satisfy in a full-length context.

title: Justin Timberlake - Man of the Woods
excerpt: A buffet of shit: Justin Timberlake’s new album is most likely the most horrendous cross-section of contemporary sounds you’re going to hear this year.

title: U.S. Girls - In a Poem Unlimited
excerpt: With In a Poem Unlimited, U.S. Girls delivers what is sure to be one of the year’s most versatile and lyrically intriguing pop albums.

title: Ravyn Lenae - Crush EP
excerpt: This latest EP from Chicago R&B singer Ravyn Lenae contains some of her boldest material yet. I’m looking forward to a full-length project!

title: Rejjie Snow - Dear Annie
excerpt: This debut studio album from Irish rapper Rejjie Snow is a bit too low-key for my liking.

title: A.A.L (Against All Logic) - 2012-2017
excerpt: Nicolas Jaar’s full-length debut as Against All Logic is one of the funkiest, most entrancing, and most cutting-edge collections of house music ever produced.

title: Screaming Females - All at Once
excerpt: All at Once boasts Screaming Females’ sharpest and catchiest songwriting in a long time.

title: Remo Drive - Pop Music
excerpt: As you might’ve gleaned from its title, Pop Music finds Remo Drive taking their sound in a poppier direction. The results are decent but brief.

title: Lil Yachty - Lil Boat 2
excerpt: Lil Yachty makes a return to form with Lil Boat 2.

title: Titus Andronicus - A Productive Cough
excerpt: Though there are a few strokes of genius on A Productive Cough, too often Titus Andronicus relies simply on the novelty of mimicking a bar band to sell the album.

title: Jean Grae x Quelle Chris - Everything's Fine
excerpt: Jean Grae and Quelle Chris have a yin and yang chemistry on Everything’s Fine, one of the smartest, funniest, and most eclectic hip hop albums I’ve heard this year.

title: Jack White - Boarding House Reach
excerpt: Jack White’s Boarding House Reach is his most unorthodox stroke of genius since going solo.

title: Wendy's - We Beefin?
excerpt: It’s no Watch the Stove.

title: Lil Xan - Total Xanarchy
excerpt: Total Xanarchy is way too drab to be even dumb fun.

title: Ruin - Plague Transmissions Vol. 1
excerpt: Plague Transmissions Vol. 1 is one of the ugliest and most standout death metal projects I’ve heard in a while.

title: Post Malone - beerbongs & bentleys
excerpt: On his sophomore album, Post Malone carves out his own niche in the auto-croon field with quality trap production, strong vocal performances, and a bit of a singer-songwriter twist.

title: Unknown Mortal Orchestra - Sex & Food
excerpt: On Sex & Food, UMO try to convey significant political messages via an inconsequential bedroom pop sound.

title: Playboi Carti - Die Lit
excerpt: Playboi Carti’s debut album is intoxicating in its simplicity.

title: Daniel Avery - Song for Alpha
excerpt: Daniel Avery’s latest effort dives headfirst into the depths of ambient techno, but comes up relatively empty-handed.

title: Kimbra - Primal Heart
excerpt: Despite being a stylistically mixed bag, Kimbra’s latest album features some of the best art pop you’ll hear this year.

title: Parquet Courts - Wide Awake!
excerpt: Not only is Wide Awake! better performed and written than any Parquet Courts album thus far, but on it the band consistently manages to make interesting artistic statements on some very difficult topics.

title: Ski Mask the Slump God - Beware the Book of Eli
excerpt: Despite its scant runtime, Beware the Book of Eli is a hilarious and killer tape that continues hinting at the Slump God’s full potential.

title: Mark Kozelek - Mark Kozelek
excerpt: Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark Kozelek Mark…

title: Nav - Reckless
excerpt: Nav’s latest is an auto-crooned void.

title: Father John Misty - God's Favorite Customer
excerpt: Even though it’s a little disappointing to hear Josh playing it so safe stylistically on the heels of Pure Comedy, God’s Favorite Customer more often than not delivers the sharp songwriting that Father John Misty is known for and admirably tackles some pretty dark and personal topics.

title: Juice WRLD - Goodbye & Good Riddance
excerpt: Juice WRLD’s brand of emo-infused trap can be great in small doses, but has amounted to a spotty full-length debut.

title: NIKI - Zephyr
excerpt: Zephyr isn’t a particularly cutting edge pop and R&B album, but with all the classy instrumentation, impassioned singing, and thoughtful writing, NIKI has a lot going for her right out of the gate.

title: Nas - Nasir
excerpt: On most tracks, not even Kanye’s excellent production is enough to save Nasir from Nas himself.

title: Big Ups - Two Parts Together
excerpt: More so than Big Ups’ two prior albums, Two Parts Together suffers from a serious lack of refreshing ideas.

title: Gorillaz - The Now Now
excerpt: The Now Now is a pleasant mood album while it’s on—especially in comparison to Humanz—but it’s still relatively low-impact.

title: Florence + The Machine - High as Hope
excerpt: Florence + The Machine exercise a bit more restraint than usual on High as Hope.

title: Kamasi Washington - Heaven and Earth
excerpt: By adhering so much to its grand formula, Heaven and Earth comes off as even more cumbersome than The Epic.

title: Dirty Projectors - Lamp Lit Prose
excerpt: Back to being a band, Dirty Projectors squanders a fair bit of potential on Lamp Lit Prose.

title: Deafheaven - Ordinary Corrupt Human Love
excerpt: Rife with post-rock cliches, Deafheaven’s fourth album contains the band’s least inspired genre-blending to date.

title: Valee - GOOD Job, You Found Me
excerpt: Valee doesn’t come through with a single flow worth stealing on his latest EP.

title: YG - Stay Dangerous
excerpt: YG tries to Stay Dangerous by going the generic trap route.

title: Melody's Echo Chamber - Bon Voyage
excerpt: Melody Prochet has bounced back with some of the freshest ideas coming out of neo-psych right now.

title: Louis Cole - Time
excerpt: Despite Louis unapologetically wearing his influences on his sleeve, Time is a solid addition to the Brainfeeder catalog.

title: Mitski - Be the Cowboy
excerpt: Be the Cowboy is arguably Mitski’s most mature release, but most of the songs feel like a faint breeze.

title: George Clanton - Slide
excerpt: George Clanton’s brand of 90s-inspired hypnagogic pop on Slide is fresh and intriguing despite the album’s concept not being taken far enough.

title: Blood Orange - Negro Swan
excerpt: Blood Orange’s latest is a dreamy, sensual, and holistic album with a message.

title: Aphex Twin - Collapse EP
excerpt: Collapse is Richard D. James’s best release since the return of Aphex Twin.

title: Russ - Zoo
excerpt: Zoo‘s songs, with only a couple of exceptions, range from boring to awful and are further weighed down by Russ’s crummy mindset.

title: Yves Tumor - Safe in the Hands of Love
excerpt: For as enjoyable as many of them are, Yves Tumor’s pop tunes and comparatively experimental soundscapes don’t really reinforce one another on Safe in the Hands of Love.

title: Lil Wayne - Tha Carter V
excerpt: Lil Wayne is in rare form on the best parts of his fifth installment of the Carter series, but bogs this album’s full potential down in a number of underwhelming cuts too.

title: milo - budding ornithologists are weary of tired analogies
excerpt: Abstract hip hop fans ought to give budding ornithologists a shot, even if it isn’t one of Milo’s standout albums.

title: Horrendous - Idol
excerpt: Horrendous takes a mighty step forward with the visceral and multi-faceted compositions that make up Idol.

title: Behemoth - I Loved You at Your Darkest
excerpt: I Loved You at Your Darkest is a solid blackened death metal album that’s occasionally marred by Behemoth overextending itself, or treading the water it waded with The Satanist.

title: Lil Yachty - Nuthin' 2 Prove
excerpt: Yeah, Lil Yachty literally sounds like he has nothing to prove.

title: Clarence Clarity - Think: Peace
excerpt: Singer/superproducer Clarence Clarity follows up his overwhelming and eargasmic debut album No Now with something a little easier to digest.

title: Rosalía - El mal querer
excerpt: Rosalía makes a fantastic transition into modern pop aesthetics without sacrificing her flamenco roots.

title: Kurt Vile - Bottle It In
excerpt: Though an improvement on his previous solo effort, Kurt Vile’s new album could have used some trimming.

title: Muse - Simulation Theory
excerpt: Muse’s foray into ’80s retro-futurism, while at times uninspired and gaudy even by the band’s standards, has resulted in their most palatable album this decade.

title: Lil Peep - Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2
excerpt: Come Over When You’re Sober, Pt. 2 features more dynamic vocal performances and a more diverse instrumental palette than its predecessor, but is still let down by shallow songwriting and bland production.

title: The 1975 - A Brief Inquiry Into Online Relationships
excerpt: A Brief Inquiry Into Online Relationships is bolder in theme and aesthetic than The 1975’s previous albums, but not all of the band’s risks pan out.

title: Onyx Collective - Lower East Suite Part Three
excerpt: Avant-garde jazz outfit Onyx Collective continues to embody the highs and lows of NYC with Lower East Suite Part Three, their most polished and straightforward set of tracks yet.

title: Soap&Skin - From Gas to Solid / You Are My Friend
excerpt: Soap&Skin’s first album in six years is sadly marred by awkward additional instrumentation and songwriting that’s lackluster compared to her previous work.

title: Sharon Van Etten - Remind Me Tomorrow
excerpt: Remind Me Tomorrow is a little all over the place in terms of style and pacing, but is nevertheless another solid set of songs from Sharon Van Etten.

title: Marquis Hill - Modern Flows, Vol. 2
excerpt: Marquis Hill and his band come through with a vibrant blend of dynamic jazz and conscious hip hop on Modern Flows, Vol. 2.

title: Deerhunter - Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
excerpt: Why Hasn’t Everything Already Disappeared? is hands-down the blandest entry in Deerhunter’s discography.

title: Ariana Grande - thank u, next
excerpt: Sweetener is no longer Ariana Grande’s strongest album.

title: Comethazine - Bawskee 2
excerpt: Bawskee 2 sounds like something a South Florida rapper would’ve uploaded to Soundcloud two years ago.

title: Panda Bear - Buoys
excerpt: Panda Bear’s latest solo outing sees his psychedelic brand of surreal folk submerged under an ocean of cascading delays and nautical vibes.

title: Kankyō Ongaku: Japanese Ambient, Environmental & New Age Music 1980​-​1990
excerpt: Light in the Attic comes out with an excellent compilation of old school ambient music from 1980s Japan, an era and location that hasn’t gotten enough shine up until this point.

title: Gunna - Drip or Drown 2
excerpt: The first leg of Drip or Drown 2 is tolerable thanks to its aquatic aesthetic, but the album quickly devolves into mega-formulaic trap rap devoid of any character.

title: Lil Pump - Harverd Dropout
excerpt: Harverd Dropout sounds more refined and slicker than its self-titled predecessor, but is all the worse for it.

title: 2 Chainz - Rap or Go to the League
excerpt: The eccentric Southern rapper 2 Chainz drops a mixed attempt at a mature album.

title: Solange - When I Get Home
excerpt: While more eclectic and adventurous than its predecessor, When I Get Home is let down by some stiff instrumentals and Solange’s inexpressive singing.

title: Matmos - Plastic Anniversary
excerpt: Even after 25 years, Matmos is creating some of the most fun and inventive electronic music you’ll hear in your life.

title: Dave - Psychodrama
excerpt: It’s hard not to nod in agreement with what Dave’s saying throughout Psychodrama, but generic instrumentals and humdrum flows don’t translate many of his good points into captivating songs.

title: Foals - Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost Part 1
excerpt: While more worthwhile than Foals’ last few albums, this first half of Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost doesn’t arouse too much excitement for Part 2.

title: The Comet Is Coming - Trust in the Lifeforce of the Deep Mystery
excerpt: The Comet Is Coming is doing its part to bring jazz into the next decade.

title: Billie Eilish - When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?
excerpt: It’s a shame that the popularity and promotion behind Billie Eilish has poisoned the well a bit, as When We All Fall Asleep is actually an artful, well-crafted, and unique pop album.

title: Stella Donnelly - Beware of the Dogs
excerpt: Beware of the Dogs is a solid indie rock and pop album thanks to Stella Donnelly’s songwriting personality, though she’s still finding her voice.

title: Show Me the Body - Dog Whistle
excerpt: New York’s Show Me the Body drops a ferocious set of banjo-backed punk ragers that are equal parts explosive and unsettling.

title: Ibibio Sound Machine - Doko Mien
excerpt: Listening to Doko Mien is like hearing Ibibio Sound Machine’s great sophomore album Uyai all over again, albeit in a slightly diminished capacity.

title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard - Fishing for Fishies
excerpt: Fishing for Fishies is a fun and eco-friendly boogie rock odyssey.

title: Kevin Abstract - ARIZONA BABY
excerpt: Kevin Abstract’s ARIZONA BABY, while sometimes messy, is an admirably intimate and candid solo project from the Brockhampton star.

title: PUP - Morbid Stuff
excerpt: PUP solidifies itself as one of this decade’s best pop punk acts with Morbid Stuff.

title: Tyler, the Creator - IGOR
excerpt: IGOR is easily one of the best breakup albums of the decade.

title: Big Thief - U.F.O.F.
excerpt: U.F.O.F. is mostly listenable—if a bit derivative—indie folk with a few flashes of brilliance sprinkled throughout the tracklist.

title: The National - I Am Easy to Find
excerpt: I Am Easy to Find returns to the dullness of The National’s early 2010s output.

title: Denzel Curry - ZUU
excerpt: ZUU blows Denzel Curry’s previous transitional projects out of the water.

title: Daphni - Sizzling
excerpt: Daphni (a.k.a. Caribou) comes through with a handful of nu-disco bangers.

title: Bill Callahan - Shepherd in a Sheepskin Vest
excerpt: Shepherd in a Sheepskin Vest is a wonderfully charming singer-songwriter project held back by a somewhat bloated tracklist.

title: Dreamville - Revenge of the Dreamers III
excerpt: Despite having similar shortcomings, Revenge of the Dreamers III is arguably the most promising posse album to have dropped in the past year or so.

title: Pi'erre Bourne - The Life of Pi'erre 4
excerpt: Pi’erre Bourne continues to dilute his sound with this latest solo effort.

title: Ed Sheeran - No.6 Collaborations Project
excerpt: Ed Sheeran’s exploitation of feature culture on No.6 Collaborations Project is second only to DJ Khaled.

title: Kim Petras - Clarity
excerpt: Clarity is a likable pop album that is carried by Kim Petras’ singing chops, though I’m hoping to hear her develop a bolder and more distinct sound going forward.

title: Blood Orange - Angel's Pulse
excerpt: There are quite a few good ideas on Angel’s Pulse; unfortunately they aren’t fleshed out enough, nor do they reinforce one another.

title: Big K.R.I.T. - K.R.I.T. Iz Here
excerpt: K.R.I.T. Iz Here is a disappointing lapse into generic trap rap.

title: Poppy - Choke
excerpt: Choke is a welcome continuation of the darker themes and genre bending of Am I a Girl?

title: Young Thug - So Much Fun
excerpt: As it happens, So Much Fun is pretty fun.

title: The Flaming Lips - King's Mouth
excerpt: The times when King’s Mouth sounds like classic Flaming Lips partly make up for the album’s spotty narrative development and pacing.

title: Bon Iver - i,i
excerpt: i,i is in a sense a refinement of 22, A Million‘s innovations, but Justin Vernon still doesn’t seem particularly interested in tying up his songs’ loose ends.

title: Alex Cameron - Miami Memory
excerpt: Alex Cameron has a talent for writing witty and smart songs about love and masculinity from a male perspective.

title: Blanck Mass - Animated Violence Mild
excerpt: Animated Violence Mild is an electro-industrial bangerfest on par with World Eater.

title: Doug Walker - Nostalgia Critic's The Wall
excerpt: And don’t get me started on the Spongebob theme song cover featuring Corey Taylor.

title: Chelsea Wolfe - Birth of Violence
excerpt: Birth of Violence‘s stripped back presentation, despite its bewitchingly dark vibe, mostly exacerbates the relatively weak songwriting.

title: Charli XCX - Charli
excerpt: Charli is a near-perfect balance of trusty pop formulas and PC Music experimentalism.

title: Brittany Howard - Jaime
excerpt: Brittany Howard undergoes an eclectic reinvention on Jaime.

title: blink-182 - Nine
excerpt: Nine will have you crying “nein” the whole way through.

title: Vivian Girls - Memory
excerpt: Vivian Girls’ first album in almost a decade is their most abrasive yet.

title: Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds - Ghosteen
excerpt: By virtue of its moving vocal performances and lyricism, Ghosteen is among Nick Cave’s finest statements—even if its sound design often leaves something to be desired.

title: Sturgill Simpson - Sound & Fury
excerpt: Sturgill Simpson’s rock experimentation on Sound & Fury sometimes goes over well; other times it goes awfully awry.

title: Highly Suspect - MCID
excerpt: The only stirring thing about listening to MCID is hearing who Highly Suspect will poorly mimic next.

title: Earl Sweatshirt - Feet of Clay
excerpt: Feet of Clay sounds like a cobbled together set of SRS-style odds and ends.

title: Battles - Juice B Crypts
excerpt: While Battles maintain their unique style of math rock on Juice B Crypts, the band sounds like a shadow of its former self.

title: Griselda - WWCD
excerpt: Griselda’s Shady debut was worth the hype if only for the collective’s unquestionable chemistry.

title: Doja Cat - Hot Pink
excerpt: Little to none of Doja Cat’s eccentricity makes it onto Hot Pink.

title: Michael Kiwanuka - Kiwanuka
excerpt: Head-scratching interludes notwithstanding, Michael Kiwanuka’s latest album is his boldest yet.

title: glass beach - the first glass beach album
excerpt: Despite some rough edges, glass beach’s debut is one of the most creative efforts in emo and power pop this decade.

title: Cattle Decapitation - Death Atlas
excerpt: Death Atlas is weighed down by its more melodic, moodier passages.

title: XXXTentacion - Bad Vibes Forever
excerpt: Bad Vibes Forever doesn’t even succeed at being an XXXTentacion album.

title: My Chemical Romance - The Black Parade
excerpt: With The Black Parade, My Chemical Romance reached the pinnacle of modern pop punk.

title: Talk Talk - Laughing Stock
excerpt: Talk Talk’s swansong is a gorgeous and timeless fusion of rock, jazz, classical, and ambient music. R.I.P. Mark Hollis

title: Stormzy - Heavy Is the Head
excerpt: Stormzy realizes his pop rap ambitions on Heavy Is the Head.

title: Mac Miller - Circles
excerpt: Circles is the finest musical send-off any Mac Miller fan could have asked for.

title: Eminem - Music to Be Murdered By
excerpt: Thanks to some creative production decisions and Eminem sounding ever so slightly less stuck in his ways, Music to Be Murdered By is a step in the right direction following Revival and Kamikaze.

title: 070 Shake - Modus Vivendi
excerpt: 070 Shake’s debut album delivers a futuristic fusion of art pop and rap, but falls short on the songwriting front.

title: Poppy - I Disagree
excerpt: I Disagree is a metal-pop crossover that pans out remarkably well.

title: Grimes - Miss Anthropocene
excerpt: For better or worse—mostly worse—Miss Anthropocene sounds as if it was made by an untrained Grimes A.I.

title: King Krule - Man Alive!
excerpt: The more direct and tuneful approach King Krule takes on Man Alive! makes it—to my ears—a vast improvement over The Ooz.

title: HMLTD - West of Eden
excerpt: HMLTD refreshes and recontextualizes a slew of post-punk sounds on West of Eden.

title: Megan Thee Stallion - Suga
excerpt: Megan’s foray into autotuned trap balladry on Suga‘s last few tracks is ultimately the EP’s downfall.

title: Loathe - I Let It in and It Took Everything
excerpt: The impact of Loathe’s ferocious riffs is sometimes dampened by the band’s obvious points of influence.

title: Disclosure - Ecstasy
excerpt: Disclosure delivers five funky and well-edited house bangers on their latest EP.

title: Machine Girl - U-Void Synthesizer
excerpt: While Machine Girl’s musical extremity remains admirable, the songwriting and mixing on U-Void Synthesizer fall flat.

title: Code Orange - Underneath
excerpt: Code Orange updates metalcore for the 2020s on their latest album.

title: Nicolas Jaar - Cenizas
excerpt: Nicolas Jaar’s second album of 2020 is an evocative set of electroacoustic vignettes.

title: Dua Lipa - Future Nostalgia
excerpt: Despite not sticking the landing, Future Nostalgia is a significant leap forward from Dua Lipa’s so-so debut.

title: R.A.P. Ferreira - Purple Moonlight Pages
excerpt: Purple Moonlight Pages is a thought-provoking self-portrait of the artist formerly known as Milo, as well as just a damn good jazz rap album.

title: Dirty Projectors - Windows Open
Thundercat - It Is What It Is
excerpt: Thundercat’s muddy mixes remain his Achilles’ heel on the otherwise enjoyable It Is What It Is.

title: Fiona Apple - Fetch the Bolt Cutters
excerpt: Fetch the Bolt Cutters has plenty of great ideas, but is sometimes betrayed by its raw presentation and quasi-experimental direction.

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Tom Waits- Bad As Me
excerpt:
Tom Waits’ latest album, rather than showing a new side to the eccentric singer-songwriter, it somewhat of a retrospective, revisiting the numerous sounds that have made this guy so “bad” for all these years.

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Cass McCombs- Humor Risk
excerpt:
The new Cass McCombs album, though I did find it to be a little middle-of-the-road, is a nice change of pace for this singer-songwriter. A good handful of the songs here have a harder rock edge to ’em, and some pretty interesting stories laced into the lyrics.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Comet Gain- Howl of the Lonely Crowd
excerpt:
Comet Gain doesn’t sound too unlike your average indie rock group, but they manage to lace their songs with some extremely memorable hooks and passionate vocals. Even though it’s nothing new, it’s difficult for me to deny.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Red Horse- Self-Titled
excerpt:
The new Red Horse album is a little front-loaded, but it still showcases some pretty intriguing noise and free improvisational sounds.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Act of Estimating as Worthless- Amongst These Splintered Minds//Leaden Thoughts Sing Softly
excerpt:
The Act of Estimating as Worthless drops a pretty worthwhile debut, comprised of sounds pioneered by some of indie folk’s favorites: The Moldy Peaches, Neutral Milk Hotel, Smog, and the Microphones.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Neutral Milk Hotel- In the Aeroplane Over the Sea
excerpt:
Finishing up classics week with a review of Neutral Milk Hotel’s seminal In the Aeroplane Over the Sea. What do you think of this album? Love it? Hate it? Why? What should I review next, eh?



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Godspeed You! Black Emperor- Lift Yr. Skinny Fists Like Antennas To Heaven
excerpt:
One of my favorite albums, which I’m reviewing in celebration of the YouTube channel hitting 50K.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: of Montreal- Paralytic Stalks
excerpt:
of Montreal’s latest album marks a slight change in sound for the Georgia psych pop band, incorporating more arranged instrumentation for a pretty classy effect.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Chairlift- Something
excerpt:
Chairlift’s sophomore LP is much more mature than the first to come from the New York indie pop band.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: First Aid Kit- The Lion's Roar
excerpt:
With some strong vocals and memorable songs, Swedish folk duo First Aid Kit retruns with it’s second album. It’s a helluva listen–even if the arranged instrumentation doesn’t have that much character to it.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Old Man Gloom- NO
excerpt:
While Old Man Gloom brings an interesting blend of ambient music and sludge metal, one side of the sound ends up feeling more interesting than the other.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Japandroids- Celebration Rock
excerpt:
On the band’s sophomore LP, Japandroids do a great job of eliciting very righteous, life-defining emotions, but don’t really surround them with anything that’s terribly engaging, musically.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Lapalux- When You're Gone
excerpt:
On the new Lapalux EP, there’s a lot of creativity to go around. Despite a lack of focus, the beats here are loaded with a bounty of different sounds and textures.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Animal Collective- "Today's Supernatural"
excerpt:
With a new album on the way in September, the experimental music outfit Animal Collective has a new track teasing toward what would be a great album.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Twin Shadow- Confess
excerpt:
Twin Shadow brings some better production and a stronger new wave aesthetic on this sophomore album, but the songwriting and lyrics seem to slip.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Rush- Clockwork Angels
excerpt:
Rush fans are pretty psyched about this new album, and I could see why. Clockwork Angels is definitely the best record the band has put out since 2000, but I’m not sure if, personally, it entertains as much as the group’s classics.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Faceless- Autotheism
excerpt:
California death metal outfit the Faceless move in a slightly softer direction on their their album, including plenty of melodic guitar passages and cleanly sung vocals.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: 2 Chainz- Based on a T.R.U. Story
excerpt: On his full-length debut, 2 Chainz embraces a popular, trunk-knocking, and Southern sound, but doesn’t supply much in the way of lyrics, personality, or entertainment.

title: The Secret- Agnus Dei
excerpt:
Though the new Secret album presents an incredible amount of energy and force, for me, the excitement quickly wears of due to a lack of skilled writing when it comes to song structures, melodies, and riffs.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Black Moth Super Rainbow- Cobra Juicy
excerpt:
Once again, despite a trademark sound the band has lovingly crafted over the course of five albums, Black Moth Super Rainbow still shows a lack of effort in the song development department.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Pig Destroyer- Book Burner
excerpt:
Though the latest effort from Pig Destroyer is undeniably an all-out riff fest, I’m not feeling the same thrilling level of intensity I typically enjoy from this genre in general.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Brian Eno- LUX
excerpt:
Brian Eno’s latest ambient effort sees him returning to his roots in the genre with albums like Ambient 1. At first, I found that pretty refreshing, and I loved the combination of piano, violin, synths, and guitar on these tracks, too. However, the album is seriously lacking in terms of new approaches or variation.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Bat For Lashes- The Haunted Man
excerpt:
On her third full-length effort, singer-songwriter Natasha Khan, a.k.a. Bat For Lashes, brings on more instrumentation and co-producers than ever to bring her moody, mystical art pop to a new level.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Game- Jesus Piece
excerpt:
Though Jesus Piece is easily the most focused album the Game has released in years, it lacks the follow-through to truly develop the concept implied by the cover art, sketches, and song titles. There’s some pretty good production on here, though.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Scott Walker- Bish Bosch
excerpt:
While Bish Bosch isn’t the strangest thing walking the planet, that certainly seems to be what he aims for on what is easily his most absurd album yet.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Macintosh Plus- Floral Shoppe
excerpt:
Chopped and screwed meets AOR, synth funk, contemporary R&B, and new age on this new album from Macintosh Plus.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Sufjan Stevens- Silver & Gold
excerpt:
SUFJAN STEVENS IS CHRISTMAS!



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Lianna La Havas- Is Your Love Big Enough?
excerpt:
On her full-length debut, UK singer-songwriter Lianne La Havas shows off a great voice, a 6th sense for melody, and a lot of promise.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Chief Keef- Finally Rich
excerpt:
On Finally Rich, Chief Keef sit back on some previously released internet hits and a few new cuts to keep the Chicago trap rap star’s name out there as we transition into 2013.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Villagers - {Awayland}
excerpt:
On Villagers’ latest album, the charismatic Conor J. Obrien leads the project into slightly more adventurous territory, incorporating electronics and ambitious arrangements in numerous tracks.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Foxygen - We Are the 21st Century Ambassadors of Peace & Magic
excerpt:
This time around, the singer-songwriter duo known as Foxygen writes an album with much more focus and cohesion than 2011’s Take the Kids off Broadway. 21st Century Ambassadors is simply one neatly crafted retro pop jam after another.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: My Bloody Valentine- Loveless
excerpt:
CLASSICS WEEK: My Bloody Valentine’s Loveless. Even 20 years after its initial release, this album still thrives as one of the strangest auditory experiences in rock and pop. Kevin Shields and company truly came together with a sonically surreal album here that still has modern experimentalists intrigued.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Comadre - Self-Titled
excerpt:
On Comadre’s new, self-titled album, the California screamo outfit releases one of the catchier albums I’ve heard in the genre for a long time.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Nosaj Thing - Home
excerpt:
Nosaj Thing’s sophomore album still has the soft, quaint sounds fans have enjoyed previously from California producer Jason Chung, but with a serious decline in the hip hop vibes that radiated so boldly off of 2009’s Drift.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: My Bloody Valentine - MBV
excerpt:
On the band’s first effort in over 20 years, My Bloody Valentine doesn’t overreach their seminal efforts on Loveless, but the band still proves they have a hefty amount of relevance and creativity to spare when it comes to shoegaze.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Unknown Mortal Orchestra - II
excerpt:
On II, Unknown Mortal Orchestra rockets past a somewhat lackluster debut with a longer album that features more variety, melody, and personality.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Darkthrone - The Underground Resistance
excerpt:
With some classic heavy metal riffage, Darkthrone comes out with their most old school album yet, which I’m sure will be a thrill to some metal fans–even if the cartoony vocals seem to poke fun at heavy metal stereotypes a bit.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Iceage - You're Nothing
excerpt:
Iceage’s sophomore full-length brings the same downtrodden, depressive ferocity that the band’s last album did, but with a bit more length and diversity. While it’s not exactly progressive, it’s still a blast–just like the debut LP.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Portal - Vexovoid
excerpt:
Australian death metal outfit Portal has a sound that impenetrably thick and noisy, and they use it to bombard listeners with an ever-changing series of riffs and dismal melodies. However, when it comes to the composition of these riffs and melodies, the album is pretty run-of-the-mill by death metal standards





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Bonobo - The North Borders
excerpt:
On his latest release, Bonobo shows more ambition with some great vocal features and vast, atmospheric production; however, too many tracks on this hour-long release don’t make much of an emotional impact.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Strokes, Matmos, Biffy Clyro, Joe Budden, Mister Lies, Sannhet, Inc., and more w/the Quickness
excerpt:
Quick and cursory reviews and mentions of some recently released albums and songs I wanted to talk about before the weekend was out. Have a nice day! Enjoy!





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Phosphorescent - Muchacho
excerpt:
On its latest full-length effort, Phosphorescent’s Americana tunes are sounding more mellow than ever due to some incredibly smooth, reverbed production.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Makthaverskan - II
excerpt:
Swedish punks Makthaverskan go a wee bit jangle pop on this sophomore album of theirs, and the results are pretty catchy.

 



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: This Routine Is Hell - Howl
excerpt:
Hailing from the Netherlands, This Routine Is Hell combines mid-paced riffs and uncompromising lyrics to create one of this years most convincing and blood-pumping hardcore releases.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Haxan Cloak - Excavation
excerpt:
The Haxan Cloak’s new, sophomore album is possibly one of the scariest sonic experiences you’ll have all year.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Soap&Skin - Sugarbread 7"
excerpt:
Austrian singer-songwriter Soap&Skin drops a new 7″ of emotionally potent tracks that should hold fans over until something more lengthy comes along.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Joey Bada$$ - Summer Knights
excerpt:
New York rapper Joey Bada$$ follows up his infamous 1999 mixtape with a collection of tracks that feel more like a sequel from Pro Era’s recently released PEEP: The aPROcalypse mixtape. Still a solid effort, though.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Classixx - Hanging Gardens
excerpt:
Get into this new album from Classixx if you’re looking for a series of breezy dance tracks with a vintage vibe, taking a load of cues from synth pop and new wave music.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Dizzy Wright - The Golden Age
excerpt: Nevada rapper Dizzy Wright’s new mixtape may have over twenty tracks on it, but not a single one of ’em stuck out to me in a significant way.

title: Ka - The Night's Gambit
excerpt:
Despite his quiet demeanor, Ka might be one of the most intense, thought-provoking, and creative MCs you run across this year.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: of Montreal - Lousy With Sylvianbriar
excerpt: of Montreal’s latest record sees the band stripping things back to some pretty base instrumentation, resulting in a sound that’s pretty similar to the band’s early work. However, Kevin Barnes proves he’s still a pretty manic songwriter, consistently delivering wordy, witty, and intense lyrics in his trademark vocals.

title: Factory Floor - Self-Titled
excerpt: Factory Floor drops a new series of austere dance tracks with this self-titled album on DFA Records.

title: The Debauchees - Big Machines and Peculiar Beings
excerpt: While the Debauchees songs and sound are admirably weird, there’s a certain stiffness in their playing that leaves me cold on a few tracks on this full-length debut.

title: Armand Hammer - Race Music
excerpt: Billy Woods and Elucid team up on Race Music to make one of the most dense hip hop albums to come out this year. With seventeen tracks laced with this duo’s esoteric lyricism, this one’s gonna require quite a few replays for maximum enjoyment and comprehension. A few shaky choruses on tracks like “Hand Over Fist” and “Renaissance Garments,” but still a rap album worth reading into!

title: CHVRCHES - The Bones of What You Believe
excerpt: Scottish synth pop trio CHVRCHES might have some really hot singles, but the rest of their debut album is a little hit or miss for me.

title: Moonface - Julia With Blue Jeans On
excerpt: The new Moonface record not only features a simple display of Spencer Krug’s vocals against his incredibly refined piano playing, but it’s also the Canadian singer-songwriter’s most personal record yet.

title: Daniel Avery - Drone Logic
excerpt: Daniel Avery assembles a diverse album of well-crafted tech house tracks that’s solid from start to finish.

title: Actress - Ghettoville
excerpt: Actress’ latest album is like a musical sketchbook filled with intimate, personal experiments with techno, house, and more.

title: Future of the Left - How To Stop Your Brain In An Accident
excerpt: If you like your rock music to have catchy hooks, wordy verses, and lots of smart-ass remarks, then I see no reason why you won’t dig the new Future of the Left album.

title: Arabrot - Self-Titled
excerpt: Norway’s Arabrot brings together elements of sludge and noise rock, gracing this hellish marriage with some of the most eccentric vocals I’ve heard all year.

title: Artificial Brain - Labyrinth Constellation
excerpt: New York’s Artificial Brain comes through with a galactic take on technical death metal on their debut album.

title: Young Fathers - Dead
excerpt: After two electrifying tapes, Scotland’s Young Fathers come through with a huge sound on this latest album of theirs, Dead. I’m not as crazy about the songs, though.

title: La Dispute - The Rooms of the House
excerpt: La Dispute comes through with a worthwhile followup to 2011’s Wildlife. While some of the stories aren’t as enthralling, the band’s minor alterations to their sound this time around makes this record worth checking out if you’ve been following them up until this point, or if you’re a general fan of post-hardcore with poetic lyrics.

title: St. Vincent - Self-Titled
excerpt: St. Vincent’s latest full-length is her most experimental yet!

title: Schoolboy Q - Oxymoron
excerpt: Schoolboy Q might not be an amazing lyricist, and his new album might have a handful of filler hooks, but Oxymoron also shows him riding a variety of beats with an impressive level of precision. Not only that, but a number of tracks here bring back the grit and vulgarity of 90s gangsta rap, and give it a progressive instrumental backdrop.

title: Sharon Van Etten - Are We There
excerpt: New York singer-songwriter Sharon Van Etten tests patience with a slow burner of a new record.

title: Chet Faker - Built On Glass
excerpt: Chet Faker brings together a few decent songs and instrumentals on this debut album of his, and while he’s a capable producer, he falls horrifically short as a singer, in my opinion.

title: Lana Del Rey - "West Coast"
excerpt: Lana Del Rey drops a new single in promotion of her forthcoming album Ultraviolence.

title: Mayhem - Esoteric Warfare
excerpt: Mayhem returns with a new record and an old school black metal sound.

title: Eyehategod - Self-Titled
excerpt: Famed sludge metal outfit Eyehategod is back with their first album in 14 years.

title: Yung Lean - Unknown Memory
excerpt: Swedish #sadboy and rapper Yung Lean drops his first commercial project here with Unknown Memory.

title: Earth - Primitive and Deadly
excerpt: With some additional vocals from Mark Lanegan and Rabia Shaheen Qazi, Earth embarks on another gloomy, psychedelic, guitar-led journey.

title: Code Orange - I Am King
excerpt: While Code Orange’s latest album might feature producer Kurt Ballou’s most crushing production yet, the band hasn’t done much to advance their writing or songcraft.

title: Dope Body - Lifer
excerpt: Dope Body releases a chaotic and somewhat psychedelic followup to 2012’s Natural History.

title: Julian Casablancas + The Voidz - Tyranny
excerpt: Fusing psychedelic pop, noise rock, lo-fi, and synth punk, this Julian Casablancas side-project is incredibly dense, diverse, and fun.

title: Andy Stott - Faith in Strangers
excerpt: Andy Stott explores more electornic subgenres on his latest full-length release.

title: TV on the Radio - Seeds
excerpt: TV On The Radio returns with a slightly more electronic sound on Seeds.

title: Pink Floyd - The Endless River
excerpt: Pink Floyd has a new album. Whaaaaaaaaaaa?

title: D'Angelo and The Vanguard - Black Messiah
excerpt: After 15 years of studio album silence, D’Angelo returns with a fantastic comeback record.

title: Ghostface Killah - 36 Seasons
excerpt: With 36 Seasons, Ghostface Killah tries to recreate the same narrative-based formula he worked with on his last album, but with only a portion of the appeal.

title: Clark - Self-Titled
excerpt: Clark heads back into familiar territory on his new self-titled album.

title: Grave Babies - Holographic Violence
excerpt: Grave Babies take a more serious, dreary, and high-fidelity approach on their new record.

title: Father John Misty - I Love You, Honeybear
excerpt: J. Tillman, aka Father John Misty, comes through with a grand, funny, and gorgeous sophomore release under this recently embraced pseudonym of his.

title: Deradoorian - The Expanding Flower Planet
excerpt: Angel Deradoorian’s full-length debut features a set of meditative, psychedelic instrumentals topped with the kind of nimble vocal work fans have come to expect thanks to her work in Dirty Projectors.

title: Health - Death Magic
excerpt: Health is back, and they’re taking it easy on the noise this time around, favoring a fusion of electronic dance music and pop on many tracks here.

title: FKA twigs - M3LL155X
excerpt: UK art pop artist FKA twigs drops a stellar EP outta nowhere.

title: Foals - What Went Down
excerpt: Despite it’s dark album cover and heavy teaser tracks, Foals’ What Went Down seems to be Foals as usual: A little depression, a little dance, a little drab.

title: Krallice - Ygg Huur
excerpt: Atmospheric black metal outfit Krallice comes through with a change of pace, delivering a speedy, tight, technical, and muscular album, but they don’t commit to the change long enough to leave a lasting impression.

title: Travis Scott - Rodeo
excerpt: Travis Scott’s ambition and songwriting translates artfully on his latest commercial effort.

title: Miley Cyrus - Miley Cyrus & Her Dead Petz
excerpt: Miley Cyrus, the Flaming Lips, Mike Will Made It and more come together for an excruciating 90 minutes of neo-psychedelic pap.

title: Battles - La Di Da Di
excerpt: Battles deliver tight performances, but lose their sense of adventure on their latest album here.

title: Dâm-Funk - Invite the Light
excerpt: Funk master Dam-Funk drops a 90-minute funk epic with his latest album.

title: The World Is a Beautiful Place & I Am No Longer Afraid to Die - Harmlessness
excerpt: Connecticut’s TWIABP is back with an even grander and more vibrant fusion of emo, post-rock, and pop punk.

title: Disclosure - Caracal
excerpt: Disclosure drops a more commercial and star-studded version of their last album with Caracal.

title: Wavves - V
excerpt: Wavves’ punk-flavored bellyaching makes V pretty hard to stomach.

title: Kirk Knight - Late Knight Special
excerpt: Pro Era’s Kirk Knight makes his commercial debut with Late Knight Special.

title: Joanna Newsom - Divers
excerpt: Singer-songwriter Joanna Newsom’s latest record is equally beautiful and conceptual.

title: Kylesa - Exhausting Fire
excerpt: Kylesa returns with an album that balances crushing sludge metal with spacey psych rock.

title: Car Seat Headrest - Teens of Style
excerpt: The infamous Bandcamp project makes its Matador Records debut.

title: Revenge - Behold.Total.Rejection
excerpt: Wanna hear something crazy?

title: Goldlink - And After That, We Didn't Talk
excerpt: Goldlink comes through with an album of rap-singing that’s seriously hard to stomach.

title: Cavanaugh - Time and Materials
excerpt: Open Mike Eagle and Serengeti come together for a new collaborative project.

title: Sunn O))) - Kannon
excerpt: Drone metal duo Sunn O))) returns with a three-part album titled Kannon.

title: Ty Dolla $ign - Free TC
excerpt: Cali singer and songwriter Ty Dolla $ign’s talents are undeniable, but I’m torn between the two halves of his commercial debut album.

title: Christian Scott aTunde Adjuah - Stretch Music
excerpt: Christian Scott and guest flutist Elena Pinderhughes come through with one of this year’s most diverse and vivid jazz albums.

title: Wiki - Lil Me
excerpt: Ratking’s Wiki comes through with a new mixtape.

title: Pusha T - King Push – Darkest Before Dawn: The Prelude
excerpt: Pusha T gets back in touch with his roots, and teases toward his next project with this mini-album that sets the bar pretty high.

title: Baroness - Purple
excerpt: Savannah, GA sludge metal outfit Baroness returns with the latest installment in their color-coded album series, Purple.

title: Radiohead - Kid A
excerpt: RADIOHEAD’S KID A! IT’S HERE! THE REVIEW IS FINALLY HERE! RADIOHEAD’S KID A! THANK YOU, TOMMY WISEAU!

title: N.W.A. - Straight Outta Compton
excerpt: N.W.A. put Compton, California on the map with this landmark 1988 album.

title: Tangerine Dream - Phaedra
excerpt: Kicking off classics week with one of prog synth’s ambient opuses, Tangerine Dream’s Phaedra.

title: Lil Ugly Mane - Oblivion Access
excerpt: “I JUST POOPED.” – Lil Ugly Mane

title: Kanye West - "Facts"
excerpt: Kanye West’s new single and freestyle, “Facts,” attempts to put Ye’s niche fashion sneaker over Nike’s Jordan footwear line.

title: Massive Attack - Ritual Spirit
excerpt: Massive Attack returns with a promising EP featuring vocal appearances from Tricky and Young Fathers.

title: Kanye West - "No More Parties in LA"
excerpt: Kanye continues his G.O.O.D. Friday series with a track featuring Madlib on production and Kendrick Lamar on a guest verse.

title: Kanye West - "Real Friends"
excerpt: Rapper Kanye West revives G.O.O.D Fridays, and delivers an introspective track exploring the shortcomings of friends and family in light of incredible fame.

title: Beyoncé - "Formation"
excerpt: Beyoncé drops a cocky new single that pays homage to her Southern roots.

title: Bloc Party - Hymns
excerpt: Bloc Party returns with one of their most conceptual albums yet, diving into themes of sadness and religion.

title: Bones - Useless
excerpt: One of hip hop’s eeriest and most elusive artists, Bones, returns with an improved sound on his latest mixtape.

title: Mr. Yote - The Terrible Tales of Scurvy Jones

title: Wild Nothing - Life of Pause
excerpt: Wild Nothing’s latest effort takes a surprisingly drab turn.

title: Charli XCX - Vroom Vroom
excerpt: Charli XCX and PC Music’s SOPHIE team up for an awesome EP.

title: Various Artists - Southern Family
excerpt: Masterminded by producer Dave Cobb, this compilation brings together some of the best and brightest voices contemporary alternative country has to offer.

title: Young Thug - Slime Season 3
excerpt: Young Thug continues his streak of redundant projects with Slime Season 3.

title: Domo Genesis - Genesis
excerpt: The commercial debut of former Odd Future member Domo Genesis barely reaches the low bar of expectations his previous tapes and features set.

title: Explosions in the Sky - The Wilderness
excerpt: Post-rock band Explosions in the Sky return with a larger instrumental palette than ever before.

title: Ash Koosha - I AKA I
excerpt: London electronic music producer Ash Koosha continues to explore vivid sounds here on his Ninja Tune debut.

title: Vektor - Terminal Redux

title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard - Nonagon Infinity

title: Skepta - Konnichiwa
excerpt: UK rapper Skepta comes through with an album that’s sure to spread the grime gospel.

title: Gorguts - Pleiades' Dust
excerpt: Death metal titans Gorguts return with an EP that delivers a monstrous 30-minute piece.

title: Post Malone - August 26th
excerpt: The abandoned lovechild of Bon Iver and RiFF RAFF delivers the best WHITEGIRLTURNUP music the Internet has to offer.

title: Modern Baseball - Holy Ghost

title: Kvelertak - Nattesferd

title: Marissa Nadler - Strangers

title: Flume - Skin
excerpt: Australian producer Flume brings the sound of wonky to a commercial audience with his latest album.

title: Xenia Rubinos - Black Terry Cat
excerpt: Singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Xenia Rubinos backs her tracks with an exciting fusion of art pop, funk, soul, hip hop, and R&B.

title: Vic Mensa - There's Alot Going On
excerpt: Chicago rapper and Roc Nation signee Vic Mensa shows off more potential than ever on his new EP.

title: Yes - Close to the Edge
excerpt: Yes’ Close to the Edge is one of progressive rock’s most fun, accessible, and triumphantly melodic albums.

title: Patti Smith - Horses
excerpt: In this classic review, I dive into Patti Smith’s amazing debut album: Horses.

title: Jon Bellion - The Human Condition
excerpt: Jon Bellion’s breakout project features a glitzy blend of pop, Pixar, and rap.

title: YG - Still Brazy
excerpt: Bompton’s own returns with an album that relives the glory days of Cali G-funk.

title: Logic - Bobby Tarantino

title: Blood Orange - Freetown Sound
excerpt: Blood Orange makes an ambitious return with Freetown Sound.

title: Red Hot Chili Peppers - The Getaway
excerpt: The Red Hot Chili Peppers get a bit of their bite back on their latest album.

title: ScHoolboy Q - Blank Face LP

title: Deerhoof - The Magic
