title: Kemba - Negus
excerpt: Formerly YC the Cynic, Kemba returns with a new name and a new album that explores some heavy, politically charged themes.

title: Gucci Mane - Everybody Looking
excerpt: Fresh out of prison, southern rap legend Gucci Mane returns with a celebratory new album.

title: Bat for Lashes - The Bride
excerpt: Bat for Lashes returns with a conceptual but underwhelming new album.

title: Noname - Telefone
excerpt: Chicago’s Noname delivers one of this year’s most heartwarming and positive mixtapes, backing her earnest rap style with beautifully jazzy instrumentals.

title: Skillet - Unleashed
excerpt: Skillet, in the wise words of Hank Hill – “Can’t you see you’re not making Christianity better? You’re just making rock and roll worse.”

title: Angel Olsen - My Woman
excerpt: Singer-songwriter Angel Olsen drops the solid, expressive record I’ve been waiting for since I heard her music back in 2012.

title: Carly Rae Jepsen - Emotion: Side B
excerpt: Canadian pop songstress Carly Rae Jepsen comes through with a surprisingly pleasing EP of leftovers from her latest album, Emotion.

title: Lil Uzi Vert - The Perfect LUV Tape
excerpt: Lil Uzi Vert returns with a mixtape whose title asserts this is the perfect Lil Uzi Vert tape.

title: Danny Brown - Atrocity Exhibition
excerpt: Danny Brown returns with one of the wildest hip hop albums ever recorded.

title: Mick Jenkins - The Healing Component
excerpt: Chicago rapper Mick Jenkins turns in a deeply flawed and shallow concept on his latest album.

title: Oathbreaker - Rheia
excerpt: The new Oathbreaker album gets off to a great, pummeling start. Then it goes soft.

title: Regina Spektor - Remember Us to Life
excerpt: Singer-songwriter Regina Spektor returns with her best set of songs in a while.

title: Nicolas Jaar - Sirens
excerpt: Nicolas Jaar experiments with vocals and a lot more on his latest album, Sirens.

title: American Football - Self-Titled (LP 2)
excerpt: American Football’s sad but nimble sound has been replaced with soft rock complacency on their new comeback album.

title: Meshuggah - The Violent Sleep of Reason
excerpt: Djent progenitor Meshuggah keeps beating a dead horse on its latest album.

title: Conor Oberst - Ruminations
excerpt: Bright Eyes frontman Conor Oberst benefits from going back to basics here on his latest solo album.

title: Jeff Rosenstock - Worry
excerpt: Jeff Rosenstock drops a pretty ambitious and conceptual follow-up to last year’s We Cool?.

title: Sleigh Bells - Jessica Rabbit
excerpt: Against all odds, Sleigh Bells has finally made an album that Anthony enjoys.

title: Czarface - A Fistful of Peril
excerpt: A Fistful of Peril doesn’t quite live up to the great expectations set by Czarface’s previous effort, last year’s Every Hero Needs a Villain.

title: Korn - The Serenity of Suffering
excerpt: Korn returns with one of their best albums since 1999’s Issues. Still can’t say I care for it, tho…

title: Emperor - In the Nightside Eclipse
excerpt: Classics Week draws to a close with a black metal landmark, Emperor’s 1994 album In the Nightside Eclipse.

title: Common - Black America Again
excerpt: The new Common album looked as if it would be a fresh perspective on the race relations in America, but it barely scratches the surface of the divides that have made so much press over the past few years.

title: Future - Self-Titled
excerpt: Future washes, rinses, and repeats on a new set of merely passable tracks.

title: Quelle Chris - Being You Is Great, I Wish I Could Be You More Often
excerpt: Though Being You Is Great… contains some of Quelle Chris’ most obtuse material, it is also the Detroit MC’s most ambitious and cohesive album yet.

title: Code Orange - Forever
excerpt: Code Orange successfully pushes the metalcore envelope on their first album for Roadrunner Records.

title: Father John Misty - Pure Comedy
excerpt: Father John Misty delivers an ambitious and grand statement on the human condition with Pure Comedy, one of 2017’s most necessary albums.

title: Spoon - Hot Thoughts
excerpt: Spoon incorporates some strange experiments into their slick indie rock sound.

title: Dirty Projectors - Self-Titled
excerpt: Dirty Projectors return with an entirely revamped sound.

title: Full of Hell - Trumpeting Ecstasy
excerpt: Full of Hell offers a fleeting thrill of sludgy grindcore on their latest album.

title: Gorillaz - Humanz
excerpt: Humanz has its share of strong performances and musical highlights, but all too often its guests are misplaced or poorly utilized and the songwriting/production just isn’t up to the Gorillaz standard.

title: Timber Timbre - Sincerely, Future Pollution
excerpt: Sincerely, Future Pollution finds Timber Timbre taking their sound in a more synthetic direction without conjuring the mood that made their past couple of albums so alluring.

title: alt-J - Relaxer
excerpt: alt-J’s third album is the UK art pop outfit’s most inconsistent yet.

title: Sinjin Hawke - First Opus
excerpt: Jersey producer Sinjin Hawke makes his full-length debut with a beautiful set of nuanced bangers.

title: Paramore - After Laughter
excerpt: After Laughter, Paramore’s first album in four years, finds the pop punk band going through a synthpop metamorphosis.

title: Kirin J Callinan - Bravado
excerpt: Australia’s Kirin J Callinan delivers one of this year’s most colorfully eccentric pop records with Bravado.

title: Katy Perry - Witness
excerpt: Witness finds Katy Perry heading in exciting new sonic and lyrical directions, but is sometimes held back by Katy indulging in safer, staler sounds and her usual cliches.

title: Roger Waters - Is This the Life We Really Want?
excerpt: Former Pink Floyd frontman Roger Waters applies the politically charged spirit of his past work to the political landscape of today on his latest release.

title: King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard - Murder of the Universe
excerpt: Murder of the Universe might be King Gizzard’s most musically and conceptually ambitious project to date, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired.

title: Elder - Reflections of a Floating World
excerpt: MA stoner rock/doom metal outfit Elder impressively reinvents itself with a more progressive sound on Reflections of a Floating World.

title: 21 Savage - Issa Album
excerpt: Issa review of the debut 21 Savage album…

title: Algiers - The Underside of Power
excerpt: Algiers blow the sophomore slump out of the water with The Underside of Power, a more intense and versatile album than the band’s self-titled debut.

title: Fleet Foxes - Crack-Up
excerpt: Fleet Foxes triumphantly emerge from hiatus with their most progressive effort yet.

title: Arcade Fire - Everything Now
excerpt: Everything Now finds Arcade Fire making a bolder and tighter move in a dance music direction than on Reflektor, but unfortunately it’s even more of a mixed bag.

title: Integrity - Howling, for the Nightmare Shall Consume
excerpt: Seasoned metalcore outfit Integrity emphasizes their metal side on the dark and diverse Howling, for the Nightmare Shall Consume.

title: Billy Woods - Known Unknowns
excerpt: Known Unknowns is NY hip hop artist Billy Woods’ punchiest effort since History Will Absolve Me. I’m talking about it with my buddy Myke from Dead End Hip Hop.

title: Oxbow - Thin Black Duke
excerpt: Thanks to Thin Black Duke‘s lavish orchestration and tour-de-force vocal performances from frontman Eugene Robinson, eminent underground rock outfit Oxbow has delivered a comeback album that leaves me lost for words for all the right reasons.

title: Aminé - Good for You
excerpt: Portland’s own Aminé sells himself short on his mellow studio debut, Good for You.

title: Kesha - Rainbow
excerpt: On Rainbow, Kesha artfully reinvents herself without losing the fun, wild energy that made her such an appealing pop figure in the first place.

title: Dead Cross - Self-Titled
excerpt: For the most part, this self-titled debut from hardcore supergroup Dead Cross offers a good balance between the genre’s original blueprint and some experimentation of their own.

title: Ski Mask the Slump God - YouWillRegret
excerpt: Ski Mask the Slump God’s outlandish and sometimes gross lyricism is sure to put off some listeners, but his animated performances left quite an impression on me over the short runtime of this latest mixtape.

title: Lil Peep - Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1
excerpt: The future of emo is looking bleak…for the wrong reasons.

title: milo - who told you to think??!!?!?!?!
excerpt: Following up on its predecessor’s sense of urgency, who told you to think??!!?!?!?! is another thought-provoking abstract hip hop album under milo’s belt.

title: Kodak Black - Project Baby 2
excerpt: Project Baby 2 offers a marginally improved Kodak Black, but mostly just more of the same.

title: Alice Glass - Self-Titled EP
excerpt: Alice Glass brings back the original appeal and energy of Crystal Castles and comes into her own as a solo artist with this self-titled debut EP.

title: Brockhampton - Saturation II
excerpt: Brockhampton offers more of the same with the second installment of their Saturation trilogy, which is fine because the group’s sound is still so refreshing and cutting edge.

title: XXXTentacion - 17
excerpt: X makes his studio debut with an angsty non-album.

title: Grizzly Bear - Painted Ruins
excerpt: Grizzly Bear returns from a five-year hibernation with a mirror image of their previous album, Shields.

title: The War on Drugs - A Deeper Understanding
excerpt: A Deeper Understanding is big on sound, but small on substance.

title: Oh Sees - Orc
excerpt: (Thee) Oh Sees is a well-oiled psych rock machine on Orc.

title: Death from Above - Outrage! Is Now
excerpt: Death from Above slay with a hard rock-inspired direction on their latest album, Outrage! Is Now.

title: Bicep - Bicep
excerpt: The electronic music tastemakers from the Feel My Bicep blog come through with some solid house music of their own on this self-titled debut album.

title: Open Mike Eagle - Brick Body Kids Still Daydream
excerpt: Brick Body Kids is Open Mike Eagle at his most low-key, but it’s also his most cohesive and emotionally potent work so far.

title: Corbin - Mourn
excerpt: Formerly known as Spooky Black, Corbin returns with a goth-tinged and minimal set of moody R&B tracks.

title: Alvvays - Antisocialites
excerpt: Alvvays’ sophomore album offers some of the best dream and jangle pop I’ve heard in years.

title: Smokepurpp - Deadstar
excerpt: Smokepurpp embodies everything the current wave of Floridian SoundCloud rap has to offer.

title: The Killers - Wonderful Wonderful
excerpt: Despite its promising singles, Wonderful Wonderful fails to come together as a cohesive artistic statement and really falls apart in the home stretch.

title: Kelela - Take Me Apart
excerpt: Kelela’s debut album is a great representation of how cutting edge the alternative R&B genre can be.

title: Lil Pump - Lil Pump
excerpt: Viral Florida rap sensation bops fans over the head with his debut mixtape.

title: Uncommon Nasa - Written at Night
excerpt: New York rapper/producer Uncommon Nasa explores potently nocturnal and political themes on his 4th studio album, Written at Night.

title: King Krule - The OOZ
excerpt: King Krule returns with a series of vague, moody musical sketches

title: Poppy - Poppy.Computer
excerpt: Poppy’s debut album is a good collection of pop songs, but doesn’t quite live up to her unique Internet personality.

title: Primitive Man - Caustic
excerpt: Doom metal trio Primitive Man returns with one of the most nihilistic albums in the genre. For anyone who enjoys some pain with their pleasure.

title: Beck - Colors
excerpt: Beck’s latest album explores the bland limits of unoriginal, sanitized, millennial pop.

title: Gucci Mane - Mr. Davis
excerpt: Gucci Mane’s latest album is long and chock-full of big-name features, but it’s little more than a glorified mixtape.

title: Fever Ray - Plunge
excerpt: Fever Ray returns in a diminished capacity with a long-awaited sophomore album.

title: The World Is a Beautiful Place... - Always Foreign
excerpt: East Coast rock outfit TWIABP returns with a simplified take on their trademark fusion of post-rock and emo.

title: Lou the Human - Humaniac
excerpt: While he does wear his influences on his sleeve, Lou the Human’s precise flows and dark sense of humor serve as a reminder of what makes underground hip hop so great.

title: Eminem - Revival
excerpt: This is bad.

title: Princess Nokia - 1992 Deluxe
excerpt: New York rapper and underground fashion icon Princess Nokia expands her 2016 EP into a 16-track monster via Rough Trade Records. One of the most eclectic rappers out right now.

title: Armand Hammer - Rome
excerpt: Elusive NYC hip hop duo Armand Hammer is back for one of the grimiest rap records of 2017.

title: Michael Jackson - Thriller
excerpt: Classics Week continues with a review of the best-selling album of all time.

title: Daft Punk - Discovery
excerpt: CLASSICS WEEK 2018 kicks off with seminal French House duo Daft Punk’s sophomore album, Discovery.

title: Charli XCX - Pop 2
excerpt: Pop 2 is another welcome collaboration between Charli XCX and the PC Music camp.

title: No Age - Snares Like a Haircut
excerpt: A decade on from their debut album, No Age is still delivering visceral and sound-rich rock music.

title: Tune-Yards - I can feel you creep into my private life
excerpt: Apart from a few bright spots, I can feel you creep contains Tune-Yards’ most uninteresting and obnoxious material to date.

title: First Aid Kit - Ruins
excerpt: Though a few missteps keep Ruins from being First Aid Kit’s best album, it’s still packed with well-written, well-performed, and well-produced folk pop songs.

title: Kero Kero Bonito - TOTEP
excerpt: Apart from the great lead single “Only Acting,” this new Kero Kero Bonito EP is pretty scant.

title: MGMT - Little Dark Age
excerpt: NY pop duo MGMT executes a fantastic return to form with the sounds of synth pop on Little Dark Age.

title: Tiny Moving Parts - Swell
excerpt: Moorhead emo outfit Tiny Moving Parts release one of their most creatively bankrupt albums thus far.

title: Tory Lanez - Memories Don't Die
excerpt: Tory Lanez is so similar to his contemporaries that it’s hard to see the point of Memories Don’t Die‘s existence.

title: SOB x RBE - Gangin
excerpt: SOB x RBE has a distinct sound and style, but things get kind of wash, rinse, and repeat over the course of Gangin.

title: Cardi B - Invasion of Privacy
excerpt: While the quality of Invasion of Privacy drops off a bit in the second half, it’s overall a promising commercial debut for Cardi B.

title: Superorganism - Self-Titled
excerpt: Though it could be more consistent and substantial, this debut album from Superorganism will probably go down as one of the year’s most creative pop projects.

title: The Neighbourhood - The Neighbourhood
excerpt: The Neighbourhood incorporates more elements of synthpop and alternative R&B on their self-titled album, which is about as drab as what came before it.

title: John Prine - The Tree of Forgiveness
excerpt: John Prine’s age and experience work to his benefit on his first album of new songs in over a decade.

title: Saba - CARE FOR ME
excerpt: Saba commendably tries to do something of depth on his sophomore album CARE FOR ME, but drowns in his influences.

title: J. Cole - KOD
excerpt: J. Cole brings a lot of heart and salient points on KOD, but it’s yet another mixed bag.

title: Princess Nokia - A Girl Cried Red
excerpt: Princess Nokia’s love for the emo scene can’t really be doubted, but A Girl Cried Red more often than not borders on unintentional parody.

title: Beach House - 7
excerpt: Beach House bounces back with their most adventurous album since Teen Dream.

title: Jon Hopkins - Singularity
excerpt: Singularity successfully reaches for the stars for a good part of its runtime.

title: Iceage - Beyondless
excerpt: Iceage dials down the abrasiveness and theatricality on the still pretty solid Beyondless.

title: Courtney Barnett - Tell Me How You Really Feel
excerpt: Courtney’s vocal performances aren’t much less humdrum on Tell Me How You Really Feel than they were on her debut, but the slightly brighter and more aggressive instrumentation this time around offers a welcome change of pace.

title: Arctic Monkeys - Tranquility Base Hotel + Casino
excerpt: With Tranquility Base Hotel + Casino, Arctic Monkeys aim for an admirably weird space-age lounge sound, but often the execution leaves something to be desired.

title: A$AP Rocky - Testing
excerpt: Testing contains some interesting ideas here and there, but they aren’t performed or organized all that well a great deal of the time.

title: BTS - Love Yourself 轉 'Tear'
excerpt: Though Tear has its consistency issues and its concept is sacrificed for the sake of having something for everybody, BTS is making ambitious and passionately performed pop music that puts many of their Western contemporaries to shame.

title: Park Jiha - Communion
excerpt: The pieces on Park Jiha’s Communion are lovely individually, but overall, the blend of sounds could have been a bit more consistent and more attention could have been paid to the album’s flow.

title: Black Thought & 9th Wonder - Streams of Thought, Vol. 1
excerpt: Backed by production from 9th Wonder and his team, Black Thought comes through with five tracks of STRAIGHT BARS on Streams of Thought, Vol. 1.

title: Kanye West - ye
excerpt: Ye paints a vivid picture of Kanye’s current state of self and, for as brief as it is, succeeds as an intimate exploration of family and mental health.

title: Rico Nasty - Nasty
excerpt: For the most part, Rico Nasty’s, well, nasty persona is enough to carry this breakthrough album. Just hoping she can show a bit more versatility on future projects.

title: Bladee - Red Light
excerpt: The only commendable thing about Red Light is that it’d be almost impossible to parody with a worse sounding version.

title: Tropical Fuck Storm - A Laughing Death in Meatspace
excerpt: The debut album from this Melbourne supergroup is rife with wry political commentary and colorful post-punk arrangements.

title: Drake - Scorpion
excerpt: Scorpion continues Drake’s streak of projects that have been padded out to oblivion.

title: Freddie Gibbs - Freddie
excerpt: Freddie Gibbs’ eponymous mixtape mostly finds the rapper spinning his wheels.

title: Zeal & Ardor - Stranger Fruit
excerpt: Zeal & Ardor’s unique blend of black metal and slave spirituals comes together in an exciting and blasphemous display on Stranger Fruit.

title: Vein - Errorzone
excerpt: Vein’s debut album offers a diverting blend of metalcore and alternative metal styles as well as its share of growing pains.

title: Let's Eat Grandma - I'm All Ears
excerpt: Let’s Eat Grandma’s sophomore album is a hodgepodge of mostly great ideas.

title: Busdriver - Electricity is on our Side
excerpt: Busdriver’s latest may appear ambitious in scope, but Electricity is on our Side only offers a less prepared version of the enigmatic rapper.

title: Trippie Redd - Life's a Trip
excerpt: Life’s a Trip has some surprisingly beautiful highlights, but Trippie Redd’s lyrics, song structures, and vocal consistency are still lacking overall.

title: Imperial Triumphant - Vile Luxury
excerpt: Imperial Triumphant effectively conveys the decadence and decay of the Big Apple with a unique blend of blackened death metal and avant-garde jazz.

title: Mac Miller - Swimming
excerpt: On Swimming, Mac Miller continues to work outside of his strengths without improving at all upon the obvious weaknesses of his previous album.

title: Eminem - Kamikaze
excerpt: Eminem falls just short of ending his career on his latest album, Kamikaze.

title: Young Thug - Slime Language
excerpt: Slime Language is an unadventurous outing for Thugger and an unimpressive showcase of YSL’s roster.

title: Noname - Room 25
excerpt: Noname’s music has only gotten even more gorgeous and charming since her breakthrough mixtape Telefone.

title: IDLES - Joy as an Act of Resistance.
excerpt: UK punk outfit IDLES return with an album that improves on the brutal and politically charged style the band delivered on their debut last year. One of the best punk albums of the decade without question!

title: Guerilla Toss - Twisted Crystal
excerpt: Twisted Crystal is all the zany pop fun of GT Ultra, but set in space and on LSD.

title: Spiritualized - And Nothing Hurt
excerpt: And Nothing Hurt is one of the more low-key albums in the Spiritualized canon.

title: 6LACK - East Atlanta Love Letter
excerpt: 6LACK continues blending into the background of the alternative R&B field on his sophomore album.

title: Hozier - Nina Cried Power
excerpt: While it’s certainly pleasant and stands out in the current mainstream music landscape, Hozier’s latest EP doesn’t offer much that indie songwriters and folk artists haven’t done better in the past couple of decades.

title: Quavo - Quavo Huncho
excerpt: If nothing else, Quavo Huncho suggests that Quavo’s dependence on Takeoff and Offset doesn’t run quite as deep as one might think. But what little appeal the album ends up having has less to do with him, and more to do with the features and variety of production.

title: Kero Kero Bonito - Time 'n' Place
excerpt: Kero Kero Bonito make their Polyvinyl debut with a pretty radical departure from the signature sound cemented on Bonito Generation. Thankfully, Time ‘n’ Place is every bit as good as that album.

title: Lupe Fiasco - DROGAS Wave
excerpt: Despite its slightly cumbersome 100-minute runtime and spotty concept, DROGAS Wave is a surprisingly solid addition to this phase of Lupe Fiasco’s career.

title: Current 93 - The Light Is Leaving Us All
excerpt: The Light Is Leaving Us All might not be particularly strange or unique in the grand scheme of Current 93’s extensive discography, but it’s nevertheless a lovely return to the band’s neofolk sound.

title: Future & Juice WRLD - WRLD on Drugs
excerpt: Two of trap’s biggest auto-crooners team up for a mixed bag of wavy, melodic bangers.

title: Sun Kil Moon - This Is My Dinner
excerpt: Mark Kozelek’s latest endeavor follows his jet-lagged excursions through Europe, but his narratives often overpower the music.

title: Metro Boomin - Not All Heroes Wear Capes
excerpt: Not All Heroes Wear Capes is a pretty cohesive listen for a producer-guided album, but it’s not fire from front to back.

title: Meek Mill - Championships
excerpt: Meek Mill’s celebratory new album ends up being a mixed bag of mostly generic pop rap.

title: Trippie Redd - A Love Letter to You 3
excerpt: A Love Letter to You 3 is Trippie Redd’s most solid project since the first one.

title: System of a Down - Toxicity
excerpt: An out-and-out masterpiece of alternative metal, System of a Down’s sophomore album was a breath of fresh air amid an ocean of cringeworthy rap rock verses and down-tuned two-note riffs.

title: Sleater-Kinney - The Woods
excerpt: Sleater-Kinney’s almost-swansong, The Woods, proved to be one of the 2000s’ most badass and essential rock albums.

title: Bring Me the Horizon - amo
excerpt: Bring Me the Horizon’s blend of pop, electronics, and what remains of their metalcore edge is surprisingly admirable on amo.

title: 21 Savage - I Am > I Was
excerpt: 21 Savage’s latest album delivers on its title.

title: Juice WRLD - Death Race for Love
excerpt: Death Race for Love delivers plenty of quality emo raps before succumbing to long album syndrome.

title: Weyes Blood - Titanic Rising
excerpt: Weyes Blood comes through with an immaculately produced and performed baroque pop album in Titanic Rising.

title: Little Simz - GREY Area
excerpt: Though GREY Area isn’t the most cutting-edge rap album out there, there’s not a spot on it where Little Simz falters even slightly.

title: Aries - Welcome Home
excerpt: Aries’ debut project is a solid contribution to the current wave of emo rap.

title: BTS - Map of the Soul: Persona
excerpt: Persona is missing the dramatic punch of BTS’s previous work.

title: Young Nudy & Pi'erre Bourne - Sli'merre
excerpt: Not much of Sli’merre‘s appeal has to do with Young Nudy.

title: ScHoolboy Q - CrasH Talk
excerpt: CrasH Talk sounds strangely dated and is a disappointingly safe effort from Q following Blank Face.

title: Lizzo - Cuz I Love You
excerpt: Though it succumbs to some trends and has a bit of a loose framework, Lizzo’s latest album is still a fantastic fusion of rap and soul music.

title: Flying Lotus - Flamagra
excerpt: Flamagra mostly sounds like a hodgepodge of ideas FlyLo has already explored on previous efforts, and what surprises it does bring are hit-and-miss.

title: slowthai - Nothing Great About Britain
excerpt: On his debut album, slowthai proves himself to be an exciting new voice in the UK hip hop landscape.

title: Megan Thee Stallion - Fever
excerpt: Fever sort of serves as a bold character portrait for Megan Thee Stallion, but more importantly, it’s catchy as fuck.

title: The Mountain Goats - In League with Dragons
excerpt: In League with Dragons is missing just about everything that has made past Mountain Goats albums so great.

title: Miley Cyrus - She Is Coming
excerpt: She Is Coming is another Miley mess.

title: Holly Herndon - PROTO
excerpt: Holly Herndon’s new album is partially aided by A.I. and features some creative, futuristic art pop pieces, but there are plenty of half-baked experiments as well.

title: Jai Paul - Leak 04-13 (Bait Ones)
excerpt: Now that it’s officially out, Anthony revisits Jai Paul’s coveted demo project that originally leaked in 2013.

title: Thom Yorke - ANIMA
excerpt: ANIMA is Thom Yorke’s strongest solo or side endeavor since The Eraser.

title: Kirin J. Callinan - Return to Center
excerpt: Return to Center finds Kirin J. Callinan putting a unique and hilarious spin on the covers album, somehow resulting in his most effective character portrait yet.

title: Purple Mountains - Purple Mountains
excerpt: David Berman’s wryly depressive (or depressively wry) songwriting seems to have only gotten sharper during his decade away from music.

title: Uboa - The Origin of My Depression
excerpt: The Origin of My Depression is one of the most harrowing offerings in experimental music this year. Profoundly disturbing and not for the faint of heart.

title: Oliver Tree - Do You Feel Me?
excerpt: Part-man/part-meme Oliver Tree continues to find common ground between pop rock, rap, and electropop.

title: Rich Brian - The Sailor
excerpt: The Sailor is by turns impressive and disheveled in its combination of so many rap and pop music styles.

title: YBN Cordae - The Lost Boy
excerpt: Even though Cordae wears some of his contemporary influences on his sleeve, The Lost Boy is a solid and promising debut album.

title: 93PUNX - 93PUNX
excerpt: With 93PUNX, Vic Mensa makes a last minute bid for the worst hip hop and rock crossover of the decade.

title: Drake - Care Package
excerpt: Many of the songs on Care Package were better off unreleased.

title: IDK - Is He Real?
excerpt: Many of the songs on Is He Real? are either too underdeveloped or lacking in a distinct voice to capitalize fully on the fundamentals and promising concept IDK brings to the table.

title: Tool - Fear Inoculum
excerpt: Tool’s comeback album Fear Inoculum is insufficient not only by the immaculate standards of the band’s past work, but by the standards of rock and metal music at large.

title: Hobo Johnson - The Fall of Hobo Johnson
excerpt: Hobo Johnson displays a rare level of vulnerability amid sharp fusions of hip hop, rock, pop, and more.

title: Ameer Vann - Emmanuel
excerpt: Ameer Vann’s comeback EP is pretty bitter and one-dimensional.

title: (Sandy) Alex G - House of Sugar
excerpt: House of Sugar is sprinkled with some brilliant and beautiful ideas, but is on the whole marred by an unsatisfying flow, dodgy songwriting, and faint lead vocals.

title: Guerilla Toss - What Would the Odd Do?
excerpt: A quick review of the new Guerilla Toss EP—it’s good!

title: Richard Dawson - 2020
excerpt: Richard Dawson outdoes himself with this modernist spiritual successor to 2017’s Peasant.

title: billy woods - Terror Management
excerpt: Terror Management‘s often humdrum production and lack of development makes it one of Billy Woods’ least gratifying works. It’s still a cut above many rappers’ best, though.

title: Uncommon Nasa & Kount Fif - City as School
excerpt: City as School lacks the focus of Uncommon Nasa’s past handful of records.

title: Mount Eerie with Julie Doiron - Lost Wisdom pt. 2
excerpt: With meandering melodies and directionless songwriting, Mount Eerie teams up with Julie Doiron for a sequel to 2008’s Lost Wisdom that pales in comparison to the original.

title: Caroline Polachek - Pang
excerpt: It’s hard to deny just how sweet, cleanly produced, and fantastical the bulk of Pang is.

title: Dan Deacon - Mystic Familiar
excerpt: Dan Deacon hones his trademark fusion of electro-psychedelia and post-minimalism on Mystic Familiar.

title: Ecco2K - E
excerpt: There are a lot of genuinely beautiful, cold, and otherworldly ideas throughout E; still, many of the songs leave me hungry for more.

title: Tame Impala - The Slow Rush
excerpt: The Slow Rush‘s deep cuts don’t deliver on the promise of its introspective and infectious lead singles.

title: Against All Logic - 2017–2019
excerpt: Nicolas Jaar’s second outing as A.A.L. is a bit more far-out than the first, and about as fantastic.

title: Royce da 5'9" - The Allegory
excerpt: Royce 5’9 is in rare form as both an MC and producer on The Allegory, an album somewhat marred by occasionally questionable messaging and a muddled concept.

title: BTS - Map of the Soul: 7
excerpt: While it has quite a few highlights, Map of the Soul: 7 is bogged down in some of the most derivative and thankless songs of BTS’s career.

title: Haru Nemuri - Lovetheism
excerpt: Haru Nemuri’s latest mini-album takes her surprisingly harmonious fusion of art pop, J-rap, noise rock, and electronica to new heights.

title: Bad Bunny - YHLQMDLG
excerpt: On his sophomore album, Bad Bunny does for reggaeton what artists like Travis Scott and Future have done for trap.

title: Caribou - Suddenly
excerpt: While Suddenly is all a bit faint in typical Caribou fashion, it’s nevertheless a sweet and heartfelt helping of indietronica.

title: Laura Marling - Song for Our Daughter
excerpt: What Song for Our Daughter lacks in experimentation it more than makes up for with its robust songwriting.

title: Yves Tumor - Heaven to a Tortured Mind
excerpt: Heaven to a Tortured Mind, a surreal celebration of soul, Britpop, and glam rock, has greater clarity and flourish than Yves Tumor’s previous work.

title: Waxahatchee - Saint Cloud
excerpt: Saint Cloud is an underwhelming take on indie country.

title: Car Seat Headrest - Making a Door Less Open
excerpt: Car Seat Headrest’s latest album is an unfortunate case of untapped potential.

title: Danzig - Sings Elvis
excerpt: By covering The King, Danzig makes us pay the ultimate price.

title: Black Curse - Endless Wound
excerpt: Black Curse displays great foundational elements on its debut album, but also runs short on ideas.

title: Charli XCX - how i'm feeling now
excerpt: how i’m feeling now is, to date, the most effective musical reflection of life during lockdown.

title: Dope Body - Home Body
excerpt: With Home Body, Dope Body improves the mixtape-esque approach of their once-swansong Kunk.

title: JME - Grime MC
excerpt: Grime MC is indeed a quality display of grime’s tenets by an MC with a lot of character and a lot to say.

title: RMR - Drug Dealing Is a Lost Art
