title: Tennis- Young & Old
excerpt:
On the sophomore effort of the indie pop band Tennis, the production and singing is noticeably better. If you dig your pop simple, then it’s worth a listen.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Gonjasufi- MU.ZZ.LE
excerpt:
Gonjasufi’s latest album shoots for many of the same sounds and ideas that made his full-length debut, but it ends up packing a less powerful punch.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: OFF!- Self-Titled
excerpt:
With its new, self-titled release, OFF! works with roughly the same formula the band delivered on its first four EPs, but with slightly less exciting results. Sightly!



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Mars Volta- Noctourniquet
excerpt:
With an emphasis on synths, edits, and effects, the Mars Volta makes the more accessible direction its been going in a lot more interesting, making this new record a colorful approach to progressive rock songwriting.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Short Audio Reviews: 05-12-12
excerpt: A series of short audio reviews touching down on new releases from Author & Punisher, Lord  Mantis, Here We Go Magic, and Orbital.

title: El-P- Cancer For Cure
excerpt:
While hip hop artist El-P is still progressing his craft as a producer on his latest studio album, some of his hooks and more conceptual tracks just aren’t sitting well with me.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Beach House- Bloom
excerpt:
On Bloom, Beach House does what they do best and continues to pen some of the best dream pop tunes out there today.



WATCH THE REVIVEW

title: Domo Genesis- No Idols
excerpt:
With some great production from the Alchemist, No Idols delivers one colorful instrumental after another with Odd Future’s Domo Genesis spitting some less-than-interesting verses.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Nas- Life Is Good
excerpt:
On his 10th album, Nas delivers a slightly modernized version of the same ol’ same ol’.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Dirty Projectors- Swing Lo Magellan
excerpt:
Dirty Projectors are sounding like a slighty more toned down version of their usual selves on this new album. While it’s certainly not a bad LP, it’s not really entertaining me on the same level their previous material has.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Wild Nothing- Nocturne
excerpt:
Improving on the project’s debut in 2010, Gemini, Jack Tatum’s Wild Nothing presents a group of dreamy, well-written, and catchy songs on its sophomore release.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: JJ DOOM- Key to the Kuffs
excerpt:
After several years consisting of a handful of features and tracks, MF DOOM is finally back with a full-length album. This time, he’s spitting over a series of instrumentals from Jneiro Jarel.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Krallice- Years Past Matter
excerpt:
On their fourth album, New York black metal outfit delivers roughly the same sound they’ve been working with for the previous three. However, despite the lack of shockingly new ideas, the band proves to hold a lot of compositional power in the methodically fine-tuned progressive black metal style they’ve made their calling card.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Swans- The Seer
excerpt:
Swans return to their freaky, challenging, twisted selves on this new new album, the Seer.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Converge- All We Love We Leave Behind
excerpt:
With more than twenty years under its belt, Massachusetts hardcore act Converge is still going strong on its latest album, All We Love We Leave Behind.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Lupe Fiasco- Food & Liquor 2: The Great American Rap Album Pt. 1
excerpt:
Though Lupe Fiasco is as sharp as ever when it comes to social commentary, production continues to be a problem for him on Food & Liquor 2: The Great American Rap Album Pt. 1.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Ondatrópica- Ondatrópica
excerpt:
Cumbia supergroup Ondatrópica puts over forty musicians to work on what might be the most essential Latin music record of 2012.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Neurosis- Honor Found In Decay
excerpt:
With Honor Found In Decay, Neurosis releases one of its most straightforward albums yet, forgoing some of the more ambitious instrumentation that’s made it onto past albums in favor of a sound that blends the heavy sounds of sludge with a bit of folk simplicity.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: 3:33- In the Middle of Infinity
excerpt:
On 3:33’s latest effort, the experimental and drone-influenced beatmusic project widens its sonic frequency, and gets pretty ambitious with a 41-minute closing track.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Miles Davis- Bitches Brew
excerpt:
CLASSICS WEEK: Though Miles Davis didn’t invent jazz fusion, he did manage to come together with one of the best albums in the genre with Bitches Brew, inviting on some of the greatest minds in the style into the studio to perform in some fiery and amazingly layered sessions.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Dead Kennedys- Plastic Surgery Disasters
excerpt:
CLASSICS WEEK: Dead Kennedys’ Plastic Surgery Disasters is easily one of the most creative, colorful, and unique hardcore albums of the 80s. With stellar performances from the band and some of the best social satire out there from frontman Jello Biafra, this record deserves much more praise than it actually gets.



WATCH THE REVIEW

title: James Blake, Pusha T, Grave Babies, Jim James, Darkstar, Lee Bannon, and more w/the Quickness
excerpt:
A group of quick, cursory reviews of albums, tracks, and other musical events that occurred this past week that I wanted to talk about a bit, which includes new stuff from James Blake, Pusha T, Grave Babies, My Morning Jacket’s Jim James, and more.





WATCH THE REVIEWS

title: Bad Religion, New Order, Just Blaze, Widowspeak, Gold Panda, and more w/the Quickness
excerpt:
Just a quick group of quick and cursory reviews of various songs and releases that I didn’t get a chance to talk about this week. Thank you for watching!





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Autechre - Exai
excerpt:
Autechre may be coming from the same cold, analytical place they usually do, but Exai shows that their skills for crafting sound are stronger than ever.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Steven Wilson - The Raven Who Refused To Sing (And Other Stories)
excerpt:
With a new solo release, modern prog rock figurehead Steven Wilson pulls together a series of tracks that feel like they function more on formulas than they do feelings.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Nick Cave and The Bad Seeds - Push The Sky Away
excerpt:
I won’t say Push The Sky Away is Nick Cave’s darkest album yet, but it’s easily one of his most depressing–so much so that Cave himself seems too shaken to engage his listeners with the same emotional potency he usually does.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Strokes - Comedown Machine
excerpt:
The Strokes continue to search for different sounds on this latest album of theirs, but it doesn’t seem they’re that picky about what the end product sounds like. The fact they sound “different” is what seems to take precedent.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Nails - Abandon All Life
excerpt:
On Nails’ sophomore release, the band makes a series of slight improvements to their already extreme sound.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Black Heart Rebellion - Har Nevo
excerpt:
The Belgian experimental rock outfit The Black Heart Procession has a pretty impressive sophomore record on their hands.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: The Uncluded - Hokey Fright
excerpt:
On a surprise collaborative album from Kimya Dawson and Aesop Rock, the singer-songwriter and MC prove their styles meld much more than they clash.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Ghostface Killah and Adrian Younge - Twelve Reasons To Die
excerpt:
On Ghostface Killah’s latest project, he’s working with composer and multi-instrumentalist Adrian Younge. Together, they create a fantastically conceptual album that’s loaded with all the b-movie thrills a Wu-Tang fan could ask for.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Kyary Pamyu Pamyu - Nandacollection
excerpt:
Japanese singer Kyary Pamyu Pamyu comes through with a second collection of tracks that are some of the most colorful and eccentric mainstream pop songs from her country.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Mac Miller - Watching Movies With The Sound Off
excerpt:
Mac Miller’s followup to Blue Slide Park is an improvement on all fronts. While it’s not gonna be one of my favs for the year, Mac is seriously reaching for the potential that I’ve felt he’s had for a while with creative production choices, better flows, and some impressive features.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Mr. Muthafuckin' eXquire - Kismet
excerpt:
Mr. Muthafuckin’ eXquire’s Kismet is definitely a bounce back from the New York rapper’s last project, which was a little too inconsistent. He brings plenty of topical tracks with grimy beats on this thing. His deep, somewhat goofy voice adds some character to these tracks, too.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Edward Sharpe & The Magnetic Zeros - Self-Titled
excerpt:
Edward Sharpe & The Magnetic Zeroes third full-length album feels even rougher than last year’s Here. However, the band is going in a slightly more retro direction, embracing the sonic palate of 60s psychedelic pop.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: letlive. - The Blackest Beautiful
excerpt:
While I think California’s letlive. has pulled together some intense performances on this new album of theirs, the obnoxious vocal harmonies and poppy appeals keeps this album’s thrill short-lived.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Toxic Holocaust - Chemistry of Consciousness
excerpt: While Toxic Holocaust’s latest album is a fast, hard-hitting combination of thrash metal and punk, I think I prefer their earlier releases due to a total lack of surprises and variety on this one.

title: MGMT - Self-Titled
excerpt: Neo-psych outfit MGMT returns with a fuzzy new album that’s got plenty of odd moments, but too few memorable ones.

title: Dawn of Midi - Dysnomia
excerpt:
The new Dawn of Midi record features some crisp production and off-kilter grooves delivered with the mechanics of a grandfather clock.





WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Sisu - Blood Tears
excerpt: Sisu’s debut full-length features some pretty sharp choruses and vocal melodies. While I’m not in love with the album, I think this project is showing a lot of promise for the future.

title: Hopsin - Knock Madness
excerpt: Cali rapper Hopsin has a tight flow and rhymes that don’t mince words. While I like the more hard-hitting tracks on this new LP of his, there just aren’t enough of them to balance out the sickening melodrama that happens on a great deal of this new LP’s songs.

title: Death Grips - Government Plates
excerpt: While Death Grips’ Government Plates might be one of the most aggressive releases to come from the experimental hip hop trio, it’s also one of their most forgettable, repetitious, short-winded, and half-baked.

title: Burial - Rival Dealer
excerpt: It’s hard to believe the three tracks on this Rival Dealer EP are actually Burial tracks, because they bring the UK-based producer’s sound in a such a different direction. We’re not getting moody, skeletal dubstep tunes on this one, people. Get ready for some auto-tuned synth pop with a boatload of atmosphere.

title: Gesaffelstein - Aleph
excerpt: Aleph has some pretty hard-hitting tech house highlights, but most of the subdued tracks just simply aren’t as engaging, and only seem like they exist to balance out the aggressive moments here–a lot of which sound very similar.

title: Real Estate - Atlas
excerpt: Like usual, the new Real Estate records is an incredibly breezy jangle pop affair.

title: Sunn O))) & Ulver - Terrestrials
excerpt: Sunn O))) & Ulver come together for a collaborative album whose recording process has been ongoing since 2008. Despite the short length of this thing, Terrestrials shows a balanced fusion of each artist’s sound.

title: Nils Frahm - Spaces
excerpt: Nils Frahm’s latest album showcases a series of live performances, pushing a lot of previously written material to the limit with longer song lengths and intense playing.

title: Onyx - Wakedafuckup ft. Myke C-Town
excerpt: After a decade-long hiatus, one of the most hardcore acts in New York hop hop return with a new album that’s backed with some solid boom bap production from Snowgoons.

title: Freddie Gibbs and Madlib - Piñata
excerpt: Indiana rapper Freddie “Gangsta” Gibbs teams up with legendary hip hop producer Madlib for one of the most essential hip hop albums of the year.

title: Lil Herb - Welcome To Fazoland
excerpt: Illinois rapper Lil Herb seems to be the hotly anticipated lyrical messiah to come out of the currently hot Chicago drill scene.

title: Cloud Nothings - Here And Nowhere Else ft. Sami Jarroush
excerpt: I collaborate with the RIO!B’s Sami Jarroush on this review of the latest Cloud Nothings album.

title: White Hinterland - Baby
excerpt: White Hinterland’s third album is the most instrumentally complex thing I’ve heard this project deliver thus far. Not only that but mastermind Casey Dienel’s voice is sounding better than ever between all of these power piano ballads and dense, soulful art pop tunes.

title: Lykke Li - I Never Learn
excerpt: The new Lykke Li record is her saddest and most heartbroken release yet.

title: Andrew Jackson Jihad - Christmas Island
excerpt: With Christmas Island, Andrew Jackson Jihad comes through with what’s essentially their pop album. While the band brings plenty of concise tracks with straightforward instrumentation, they mostly lack the emotional impact of previous material–the instrumental finesse, too.

title: Ought - More Than Any Other Day
excerpt: Montreal’s Ought displays a pretty wide set of influences on this debut record of theirs, including experimental folk rock to tracks that blend sounds of Midwest emo with the dismal emotions of bands like Slint.

title: Lana Del Rey - Ultraviolence
excerpt: Behold, the epitome of superficial nostalgia!

title: Trash Talk - No Peace
excerpt: Trash Talk’s latest album might have ferocity, but the music does little to capture the hardcore punk imagination.

title: Lone - Reality Testing
excerpt: The approach Lone took to his latest record here is shockingly basic, and a disheartening departure from the vibrant, upbeat instrumentals on his last LP.

title: Mellowhype - INSA
excerpt: Mellowhype’s latest project shows an enjoyable increase in technical skill since their last full-length affair–even if the end the result is sort of generic.

title: Wolves In the Throne Room - Celestite
excerpt: Wolves In the Throne Room come through with an electronic and ambient change of pace on this new record of theirs.

title: Ty Segall - Manipulator
excerpt: Ty Segall’s latest album is one of his most methodically assembled releases yet.

title: Armand Hammer - Furtive Movements
excerpt: Armand Hammer drops a post-album EP of fan-pleasing odds ‘n’ ends.

title: Weezer - Everything Will Be Alright In The End
excerpt: Weezer writes some of its best–and worst–songs in years.

title: Shellac - Dude Incredible
excerpt: The new Shellac album is decent, but falls disappointingly short of the reaction “Dude, incredible!”

title: Aphex Twin - Syro
excerpt: After 13 years of studio album silence, Aphex Twin makes a mild return.

title: Big K.R.I.T. - Cadillactica
excerpt: Big K.R.I.T.’s second commercial project, much like his last, leaves much to be desired.

title: Foxygen - ...And Star Power
excerpt: Foxygen does a complete 180 on their new record, saying goodbye to the clean production on their last album, and heading into lo-fi territory. However, they throw out any semblance of good songwriting in the process.

title: I Am Your Destruction - Self-Titled
excerpt: The new IAYD record brings together 8-bit synth timbres and with the kinds of “drops” popular in present-day EDM.

title: Dean Blunt - Black Metal
excerpt: UK singer-songwriter and musical oddball Dean Blunt releases an album that’s difficult to put into words. While simple in composition and sloppy in execution, the album still manages to draw up some real feelings of isolation, melancholy, and frustration.

title: Mr. Oizo - The Church
excerpt: Mr. Oizo’s new album for Brainfeeder Records takes on a punchier, more West Coast sound.

title: Dope Body - Kunk
excerpt: Baltimore’s Dope Body drops a short but exciting album of new material based off noisy, intense improvs.

title: Dr. Dre - Compton: A Soundtrack
excerpt: Dr. Dre is back! Dr. Dre is back! Dr. Dre is back!

title: The Underachievers - Evermore: The Art of Duality
excerpt: The Underachievers explore the duality of life on this new two-part album.

title: The Libertines - Anthems for Doomed Youth
excerpt: The Libertines drop a comeback record! Woo! Woo!

title: Whitey Morgan and the 78's - Sonic Ranch
excerpt: Whitey Morgan’s latest record delivers an authentic outlaw country feel with a modern clarity and punch coming through on the production.

title: Deafheaven - New Bermuda
excerpt: Deafheaven returns with a set of ambitious, dynamic songs mixing black metal and indie-flavored instrumental rock.

title: Drake & Future - What a Time to Be Alive
excerpt: While a few tracks feature an equal and exciting marriage of Champagne Papi and Future Hendrix, most of what’s here feels like DS2 runoff with a solid Drake feature.

title: Oneohtrix Point Never - Garden of Delete
excerpt: Oneohtrix Point Never returns with a mind-bending set of tracks on Garden of Delete.

title: The Game - The Documentary 2.5
excerpt: The second installment of the Game’s sequel to 2005’s The Documentary turns out more focused and emotive than its predecessor.

title: Freddie Gibbs - Shadow of a Doubt
excerpt: Freddie Gibbs comes through with a new project that’s equally moody and grimy.

title: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard - Paper Mâché Dream Balloon
excerpt: Melbourne’s King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard delivers an album of poppy, psychedelic, acoustic numbers on their latest project here.

title: Anna von Hausswolff - The Miraculous
excerpt: Sweden’s Anna von Hausswolff expands her sound into experimental and progressive rock on her latest album of atmospheric organ dirges.

title: Kendrick Lamar and J. Cole - "Black Friday"
excerpt: Kendrick Lamar and J. Cole trade beats and remixes on these two new tracks.

title: Arca - Mutant
excerpt: Venezuelan experimental electronic music producer Arca expands on many of the sonic themes forged on her full-length debut last year.

title: Archy Marshall - A New Place 2 Drown
excerpt: Archy Marshall, a.k.a. King Krule, returns with a new album of downtrodden, spacey hip hop motifs that bore more than they inspire.

title: Erykah Badu - But You Caint Use My Phone
excerpt: Erykah Badu returns with a mix of smooth, phone-themed soul and R&B tracks.

title: Ty Segall - Emotional Mugger
excerpt: Garage rock titan Ty Segall is back with what’s probably his most twisted album yet.

title: David Bowie - ★ (Blackstar)
excerpt: Entertainment icon David Bowie turns his death into an awe-inspiring concept album.

title: Slint - Spiderland
excerpt: Slint’s Spiderland is a depressingly intense pinnacle of creativity for a variety of underground rock styles.

title: Daughter - Not to Disappear
excerpt: The UK indie outfit Daughter comes through with a painfully drab sophomore record.

title: Anderson .Paak - Malibu
excerpt: Singer-songwriter Anderson .Paak comes through with a formidable breakout album that fuses elements of soul, hip hop, pop, funk, and more.

title: Death Grips - "Hot Head"
excerpt: Elusive experimental hip hop trio Death Grips hands over the first single from their forthcoming album.

title: Young Thug - I'm Up
B.o.B - "Flatline" & Tyson - "Flat to Fact"
excerpt: B.o.B. and Neil Degrasse Tyson’s nephew go back and forth over Earth’s dimensions on a couple of new diss tracks.

title: Kanye West - The Life of Pablo
excerpt: Kanye West attempts to sell disjointed and incomplete as a concept on his latest album.

title: Future - EVOL
excerpt: Once again, Atlanta rapper and auto-tuned crooner Future delivers a cool aesthetic with little substance.

title: The 1975 - I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful Yet So Unaware of It
excerpt: UK pop rock outfit The 1975 returns with the most bloated pop record I’ve heard so far this year. A few decent tracks on it, tho.

title: Kendrick Lamar - untitled unmastered.
excerpt: kendrick lamar. new album. untitled. unmastered.

title: Babymetal - Metal Resistance
excerpt: Japan’s Babymetal continues fusing J-pop and heavy metal on their sophomore album.

title: Drake - "Pop Style" & "One Dance"
excerpt: These songs: Not good.

title: Flatbush Zombies - 3001: A Laced Odyssey
excerpt: Flatbush Zombies come through with their most lax, spacey project yet on their commercial debut, 3001: A Laced Odyssey.

title: A$AP Ferg - Always Strive and Prosper
excerpt: A$AP Ferg releases a painfully commercial sophomore album.

title: M83 - Junk
excerpt: M83 returns with an album with more hollow nostalgia than quality tunes.

title: Kaytranada - 99.9%
excerpt: Montreal producer Kaytranada shows off his versatility and a star-studded feature list on this XL Recordings debut.

title: Chance the Rapper - Coloring Book
excerpt: Chance the Rapper returns with a new mixtape fusing the sounds of jazz, hip hop, and gospel.

title: Beyoncé - Lemonade
excerpt: Beyoncé drops her most conceptual and mature album yet — as well as what’s likely to be the best pop record of the year.

title: Moonsorrow - Jumalten Aika
excerpt: Moonsorrow deliver another installment of triumphant, grand, epic folk metal with their latest album.

title: Car Seat Headrest - Teens of Denial
excerpt: Singer-songwriter Will Toledo pushes bedroom pop and lo-fi rock to the next level on the new Car Seat Headrest album.

title: Olga Bell - Tempo
excerpt: Brooklyn-based singer, songwriter, and producer Olga Bell delivers an interesting blend of art pop and electronic music on her latest record.

title: PUP - The Dream Is Over
excerpt: At its best, the new PUP album is a clever, witty piece of modern pop punk, At its worst, it’s a temper tantrum.

title: David Bowie - The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
excerpt: CLOSING OUT CLASSICS WEEK WITH AN AMAZING ALBUM. ZIGGY STARDUST. DAVID BOWIE. ENJOY.

title: Nirvana - In Utero
excerpt: In this classic review, I take on the final album from seminal grunge outfit Nirvana.

title: Nas - Illmatic
excerpt: In this new classic review, I dive into one of the East Coast’s most legendary rap records: Nas’ Illmatic.

title: Bones - PaidProgramming2
excerpt: Prolific and eerie Cali rapper Bones returns with the sequel to his 2013 PaidProgramming mixtape.

title: DJ Khaled - Major Key
excerpt: DJ Khaled embraces the meme and drops some decent tracks on his new album.

title: 21 Savage & Metro Boomin - Savage Mode
excerpt: Hey, the beats are decent, tho…

title: Rae Sremmurd - Sremmlife 2
excerpt: Do you say “IT’S LIT” a lot in daily conversation? If so, you’ll dig this album even more than I did!

title: PartyNextDoor - P3
excerpt: OVO’s PartyNextDoor returns with some slight improvements on his spacey R&B sound.

title: Show Me the Body - Body War
excerpt: New York’s Show Me the Body deliver one of the most riotous and creative albums of 2016.

title: Thee Oh Sees - A Weird Exits
excerpt: Prolific garage rock outfit Thee Oh Sees drop one of their best records in years.

title: Glass Animals - How to Be a Human Being
excerpt: UK art pop outfit Glass Animals is back with a sophomore album! The band has come through with set of punchy, colorful instrumentals that could have used some more vibrant vocal performances.

title: Ka - Honor Killed the Samurai
excerpt: Brownsville’s own Ka does it again with a tragic set of the most chilling hip hop songs you’ll hear this year. Bars abound!

title: AJJ - The Bible 2
excerpt: AJJ returns with a new name, uh, or abbreviation, and a slightly conceptual angle on their latest record.

title: The Dillinger Escape Plan - Dissociation
excerpt: The Dillinger Escape Plan goes down swinging on their final album.

title: NxWorries - Yes Lawd!
excerpt: Anderson .Paak and Knxwledge return with a fruitful full-length collaboration.

title: clipping. - Splendor & Misery
excerpt: The experimental hip hop trio clipping. returns with an intriguing concept album.

title: Lady Gaga - Joanne
excerpt: Lady Gaga’s rootsier sound and image on Joanne is a welcome change of pace, though she doesn’t always commit to the new direction.

title: The Game - 1992
excerpt: Compton rapper The Game returns with a partially fulfilled concept album about his early days.

title: Tove Lo - Lady Wood
excerpt: This new Tove Lo album is some of the blandest and unsexiest pop music I’ve heard all year.

title: Wormrot - Voices
excerpt: Wormrot goes the distance with a new set of abrasive and diverse tracks that run the extreme music gamut.

title: Justice - Woman
excerpt: The French electronic music duo returns with their weakest crop of songs yet.

title: Bruno Mars - 24K Magic
excerpt: Pop phenom Bruno Mars throws it back to the sounds of synth funk and R&B from 30 years ago. The result is his best album yet.

title: J. Cole - 4 Your Eyez Only
excerpt: J. Cole returns with a personal set of vignettes on 4 Your Eyez Only.

title: The Wytches - All Your Happy Life
excerpt: On All Your Happy Life, UK garage rock outfit The Wytches hits a bit of a sophomore slump.

title: Injury Reserve - Floss
excerpt: Arizona’s Injury Reserve threatens the rap establishment with one of the most exciting tapes in the underground right now.

title: Post Malone - Stoney
excerpt: Post Malone proves his status as a one-hit wonder with his commercial debut, Stoney.

title: Ab-Soul - Do What Thou Wilt.
excerpt: TDE’s living lyrical conundrum, Ab-Soul, returns for one of his most dense albums yet.

title: Little Simz - Stillness in Wonderland
excerpt: The UK’s Little Simz returns with a concept album about making the transition from ignorance to awareness.

title: Kid Cudi - Passion, Pain & Demon Slayin'
excerpt: Kid Cudi returns with an album that plays more toward his strengths. I use the word “strengths” loosely.

title: Iron Reagan - Crossover Ministry
excerpt: Talking with my dude Myke C-Town about this new Iron Reagan album, the Virginian crossover thrash outfit’s second outing for Relapse Records.

title: Big Sean - I Decided
excerpt: With I Decided, Big Sean releases an album that gives me more to say than just “no.”

title: Bedwetter - Flick Your Tongue Against Your Teeth and Describe the Present
excerpt: Travis Miller’s first volume of music as Bedwetter is a harrowing statement on mental health… when Travis is rapping.

title: Sun Kil Moon - Common as Light and Love Are Red Valleys of Blood
excerpt: When Mark Kozelek arrives, baby, he arrives.

title: Lupe Fiasco - DROGAS Light
excerpt: DROGAS Light is one of Lupe Fiasco’s better attempts at making an album with pop appeal, though it still pales in comparison to his more progressive work like Tetsuo & Youth.

title: Jonwayne - Rap Album Two
excerpt: With RA2, Jonwayne delivers a disheveled set of alternative hip hop tracks that have potent senses of humor and emotion.

title: King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard - Flying Microtonal Banana
excerpt: The new King Gizzard album, while not a thorough experiment in microtonal tuning, is a fun and intense psych rock experience.

title: Future - HNDRXX
excerpt: Future showcases his softer, “sexier” side on HNDRXX, his worst album yet.

title: Blanck Mass - World Eater
excerpt: Blanck Mass makes a grand, industrial-flavored return with World Eater.

title: Charli XCX - Number 1 Angel
excerpt: Charli XCX continues to turn pop on its head with PC Music’s best producers.

title: Remo Drive - Greatest Hits
excerpt: Remo Drive keeps the torch lit for emo with their promising debut.

title: Your Old Droog - Packs
excerpt: With PACKS, Brooklyn’s Your Old Droog continues to flex his lyrical muscles on his most focused album yet.

title: Idles - Brutalism
excerpt: Brutalism, the debut album by UK five piece IDLES, may not reinvent the punk rock wheel but is loaded with some of the most fiery performances and brutally honest lyrics I’ve heard in years.

title: Kodak Black - Painting Pictures
excerpt: Painting Pictures is Kodak Black’s most well-produced project yet, but his lyrics and delivery still leave a lot to be desired.

title: Mastodon - Emperor of Sand
excerpt: On Emperor of Sand, Mastodon pads out rehashed ideas from their last several albums with alt-rock choruses that went out of style with the 90s.

title: Freddie Gibbs - You Only Live 2wice
excerpt: Freddie Gibbs makes a rushed return with You Only Live 2wice.

title: The Magnetic Fields - 50 Song Memoir
excerpt: While not a full commitment to its titular concept, 50 Song Memoir is The Magnetic Fields’ most charming and ambitious album in over a decade.

title: Future Islands - The Far Field
excerpt: The Far Field, the fifth album from NC synthpop trio Future Islands, is a serious case of musical déjà vu.

title: Harry Styles - Self-Titled
excerpt: Harry Styles’ solo debut falls way short of its quality singles. Also HOW IS THERE DAD ROCK ON THIS THING?

title: Mac DeMarco - This Old Dog
excerpt: Mac DeMarco matures as a songwriter on This Old Dog, his best album since 2.

title: Logic - Everybody
excerpt: Logic’s new album puts the “mess” in “message.”

title: The Mountain Goats - Goths
excerpt: The Mountain Goats’ latest is a gothic-themed concept album, a foray into the world of guitar-less music, and one of the greatest testaments to John Darnielle’s chops as a storyteller.

title: Brockhampton - Saturation
excerpt: On Saturation, Brockhampton jells in a way no other group their size has in quite some time. Definitely my frontrunner for hip hop project of the year at the moment.

title: (Sandy) Alex G - Rocket
excerpt: With Rocket, Philly singer-songwriter Alex G delivers an album that’s a bit more adventurous than his previous effort, but also a lot more inconsistent.

title: Vince Staples - Big Fish Theory
excerpt: Vince Staples’ Big Fish Theory is the Long Beach rapper’s most eclectic project yet, but still exposes major songwriting deficiencies.

title: Lorde - Melodrama
excerpt: On her sophomore album Melodrama, Lorde makes a few Top 40 concessions, but shows a ton of promise with the stylistic and formal risks she does take.

title: Shabazz Palaces - Quazarz
excerpt: Shabazz Palaces return with deeply flawed twin concept albums.

title: Lana Del Rey - Lust for Life
excerpt: While Lust for Life might be Lana Del Rey’s weakest attempt at reconciling her old school and new school influences, it’s also the first time I’ve come away from one of her albums with more highlights than lowlights.

title: Guerilla Toss - GT ULTRA
excerpt: Thanks to some clearer production, more up-front performances, and a zany new wave influence, GT ULTRA is the most I’ve ever enjoyed a Guerilla Toss album.

title: wifisfuneral - Boy Who Cried Wolf
excerpt: Despite a few questionable features, wifisfuneral’s latest mixtape shows the potential of the current rap landscape on SoundCloud.

title: Everything Everything - A Fever Dream
excerpt: The latest Everything Everything album finds the UK art pop outfit taking their songwriting in a moodier and somewhat more conventional direction.

title: Lil B - Black Ken
excerpt: At over 90 minutes, Lil B’s “first official mixtape” is chock-full of freewheeling, creative highs; as well as lows that range from mundane to annoying.

title: The National - Sleep Well Beast
excerpt: Sleep Well Beast is The National’s most vibrant and engaging set of songs in years.

title: Trippie Redd - A Love Letter to You 2
excerpt: At its best, A Love Letter to You 2 is emotionally stirring, cutting edge, and tuneful, but there are just as many moments I can’t stand.

title: Iglooghost - Neō Wax Bloom
excerpt: Iglooghost makes his full-length Brainfeeder debut with the impressive and fantastical Neō Wax Bloom.

title: Injury Reserve - Drive It Like It's Stolen EP
excerpt: Injury Reserve drops a solid, relatively low-key EP.

title: Skepta - Vicious
excerpt: Skepta’s new EP starts strong enough and even offers a miraculous banger featuring the Based God himself, but it instantly takes a nosedive in the second half.

title: 21 Savage, Offset & Metro Boomin - Without Warning
excerpt: 21 Savage, Offset, and Metro Boomin teamed up for a solid collaborative album just in time for Halloween.

title: Big K.R.I.T. - 4eva Is a Mighty Long Time
excerpt: The Mississippi quadruple threat is back with an epic double album that puts him at a new level.

title: Quality Control - Control the Streets, Vol. 1
excerpt: Migos and other stars from the Quality Control label assemble for a new, massive compilation.

title: Yung Lean - Stranger
excerpt: Cloud rap sorcerer Yung Lean returns with his most enjoyable and aesthetically mature album to date.

title: Brockhampton - Saturation III
excerpt: West Coast boy band Brockhampton round out their Saturation trilogy with their most versatile and melodic album yet.

title: Big Sean & Metro Boomin - Double or Nothing
excerpt: Atlanta’s own Metro Boomin crafts some of his best production yet for this new collaboration with Big Sean, but the Detroit resident fails to deliver.

title: Travis Scott & Quavo - Huncho Jack, Jack Huncho
excerpt: Huncho Jack is a collaboration between two of the hottest rappers out right now, but the end result is a bit too predictable and uniform.

title: JPEGMAFIA - Veteran
excerpt: Veteran is sure to be one of the most in-your-face, off-the-wall and creative rap projects of 2018.

title: Logic - Bobby Tarantino II
excerpt: Despite the bouncy production, good feature spots, and Logic’s technical ability, Bobby Tarantino II is just as inconsequential as its predecessor.

title: Anna von Hausswolff - Dead Magic
excerpt: Dead Magic is Swedish singer-songwriter and organist Anna von Hausswolff’s best work to date.

title: 6ix9ine - Day69
excerpt: 6ix9ine brings a ton of aggression and energy to his debut mixtape, but lacks the versatility, charisma, and ear for interesting production to carry an entire project… even one that’s just 27 minutes.

title: PRhyme - PRhyme 2
excerpt: Royce da 5’9″ and DJ Premier’s second outing as PRhyme is a more versatile effort than the first, with Premo’s varied production stealing the show.

title: Young Fathers - Cocoa Sugar
excerpt: Cocoa Sugar is one of Young Fathers’ milder releases.

title: XXXTENTACION - ?
excerpt: X makes some improvements on the mixing, singing, and songwriting fronts with ?, but the album is still a mixed bag consisting mainly of half-baked song ideas.

title: CZARFACE & MF DOOM - Czarface Meets Metal Face
excerpt: Though a bit predictable and restrained, Czarface Meets Metal Face is a solid collaboration that’s a cut above both parties’ most recent work.

title: The Voidz - Virtue
excerpt: The Voidz’s everything-and-the-kitchen-sink approach to rock music results in a vibrant sophomore album.

title: Panopticon - The Scars of Man on the Once Nameless Wilderness
excerpt: The two-disc Scars of Man finds Panopticon separating the black metal and American folk elements of his music, rendering it generic.

title: Flatbush Zombies - Vacation in Hell
excerpt: Vacation in Hell has its share of great songs, but many of the deep cuts find the Zombies punching below their weight.

title: SOPHIE - Oil of Every Pearl's Un-Insides
excerpt: Though structurally jarring, SOPHIE’s full-length debut is an unforgettable and potentially DNA-altering pop album.

title: Tierra Whack - Whack World
excerpt: The debut album from Philly hip hop artist Tierra Whack is an endearing set of pop rap and alternative R&B miniatures.

title: Nine Inch Nails - Bad Witch
excerpt: The level of artistic freedom Trent and Atticus give themselves on the somewhat uneven Bad Witch is more exciting than just about any Nine Inch Nails release since 2008.

title: Death Grips - Year of the Snitch
excerpt: Death Grips is online.

title: Nicki Minaj - Queen
excerpt: Nicki Minaj still has her energy, technical ability, and sharp lyricism going for her, but too often on Queen these are drowned out by generic production and horrid features.

title: 88rising - Head in the Clouds
excerpt: Head in the Clouds blends into the current wave of trap-flavored pop rap a little too well.

title: Jay Rock - Redemption
excerpt: Sorry to run with the obvious music critic quip, but it is pretty hard to hear what’s so redeeming about Redemption.

title: $uicideBoy$ - I Want to Die in New Orleans
excerpt: $uicideBoy$’s debut album delivers a dark and grimy vibe, but the duo hasn’t evolved much artistically since they first started turning heads on Soundcloud.

title: Armand Hammer - Paraffin
excerpt: Billy Woods and Elucid team up again as Armand Hammer for one of the year’s best abstract hip hop albums.

title: Oh Sees - Smote Reverser
excerpt: Though it’s a pretty solid work of modern psych, Smote Reverser isn’t the wall-to-wall excitement that Oh Sees’ last few albums have been.

title: Logic - YSIV
excerpt: Logic is, as always, well-intentioned and likable on YSIV, but his music remains middle-of-the-road.

title: BROCKHAMPTON - iridescence
excerpt: The all-American boyband makes its major label debut with an album that shows emotional and creative maturation despite occasionally gimmicky production and some members getting outshined by others.

title: Lil Baby & Gunna - Drip Harder
excerpt: YSL and Quality Control really should’ve kept these two on the bench.

title: twenty one pilots - Trench
excerpt: Twenty One Pilots take their catchy songwriting, genre blending, and emotional lyricism up a few notches on Trench.

title: Little Big - Antipositive, Pt. 2
excerpt: Russian dance music outfit Little Big continue to drop supremely weird, provocative rave music.

title: Open Mike Eagle - What Happens When I Try to Relax
excerpt: What Happens When I Try to Relax is an interesting mini-chapter in the ongoing OME saga.

title: Vince Staples - FM!
excerpt: FM!‘s fun concept begs for a longer runtime, but even at 22 minutes the project has plenty to offer with its quality beats, flows, hooks, and lyrics.

title: Daughters - You Won't Get What You Want
excerpt: Daughters return with the most effectively terrifying album I’ve heard all decade.

title: Tyler, the Creator - Music Inspired by Illumination & Dr. Seuss' The Grinch
excerpt: Tyler, the Creator leaves an awkward and weakly assembled Christmas EP under the tree.

title: Jaden Smith - The Sunset Tapes: A Cool Tape Story
excerpt: The Sunset Tapes just sounds like it doesn’t matter.

title: Poppy - Am I a Girl?
excerpt: Poppy and her collaborators have gotten a lot better at working her persona into her music and crafting creative pop songs since last year’s Poppy.Computer.

title: Earl Sweatshirt - Some Rap Songs
excerpt: Some Rap Songs is Earl Sweatshirt’s most emotionally intense and artistically defined project yet.

title: J.I.D - DiCaprio 2
excerpt: With sick flows and a versatile delivery, J.I.D’s latest effort is one of the rawest and most lyrically refined rap albums of the year.

title: Black Thought & Salaam Remi - Streams of Thought, Vol. 2
excerpt: Despite its occasional lyrical missteps and production that’s maybe a little too standard for Black Thought, this second Streams of Thought EP is nearly as solid as the first.

title: XXXTentacion - Skins
excerpt: Skins is one of the year’s least gratifying albums, but out of everyone involved in its creation, X is probably the least at blame.

title: Cannibal Ox - The Cold Vein
excerpt: The Cold Vein pulled the sounds of East Coast rap music into the future and opened the floodgates for a new strain of leftfield hip hop.

title: The Postal Service - Give Up
excerpt: The Postal Service’s only album stands as an indietronic masterpiece and one of the best albums of the aughts.

title: James Blake - Assume Form
excerpt: Despite being bookended by a few awkward detours, Assume Form contains James Blake’s best writing and production since the earlier part of this decade.

title: Bad Bunny - X 100PRE
excerpt: The full-length debut from Latin trap popularizer Bad Bunny mostly sounds standard even in the context of stateside pop rap.

title: Blu & Oh No - A Long Red Hot Los Angeles Summer Night
excerpt: A Long Red Hot Los Angeles Summer Night contains quite a bit of Blu and Oh No’s best work to date.

title: Xiu Xiu - Girl with Basket of Fruit
excerpt: Xiu Xiu delivers what might be its most adventurous and harrowing album to date… which is saying a lot.

title: LCD Soundsystem - Electric Lady Sessions
excerpt: While much of your enjoyment of Electric Lady Sessions will depend on your enjoyment of American Dream, that material does benefit from the more in-the-moment sound here.

title: American Football - American Football (LP3)
excerpt: Following a disappointing comeback album in 2016, American Football shows promise once again with the dreamier LP3.

title: Flume - Hi This Is Flume
excerpt: Flume’s full-length followup to 2016’s Skin takes a very welcome turn for the experimental.

title: Anderson .Paak - Ventura
excerpt: Ventura is much more than a set of Oxnard leftovers.

title: Billy Woods & Kenny Segal - Hiding Places
excerpt: Hiding Places is Billy Woods’ most personally cutting project so far.

title: Logic - Supermarket
excerpt: Supermarket is Logic’s very own Speedin’ Bullet 2 Heaven.

title: Beyoncé - HOMECOMING: The Live Album
excerpt: Beyoncé pulls out all the stops on HOMECOMING, a live album of epic proportions.

title: Dos Monos - Dos City
excerpt: Dos Monos’ strange and intense sound is certainly unique, though it becomes a bit of a crutch as Dos City wears on.

title: Slauson Malone - A Quiet Farwell, 2016–2018
excerpt: A Quiet Farwell is an inventive and consistently stimulating collage of underground hip hop and various strands of abstract music.

title: Rico Nasty & Kenny Beats - Anger Management
excerpt: Anger Management finds Rico Nasty continuing to be one of the boldest voices in the current rap landscape, but the project’s brevity is unfortunately to its detriment.

title: Rammstein - Untitled
excerpt: Rammstein’s first studio album in 10 years falls apart after a promising first leg.

title: Injury Reserve - Injury Reserve
excerpt: Injury Reserve’s debut studio album isn’t quite as consistent as the trio’s mixtapes, but is nevertheless a cut above most of what you’ll find in today’s rap field.

title: Mac DeMarco - Here Comes the Cowboy
excerpt: Mac DeMarco pares his songwriting down to something more minimal on Here Comes the Cowboy, losing a lot of personality along the way.

title: Baroness - Gold & Grey
excerpt: Gold & Grey‘s awful production overshadows its handful of songwriting peaks.

title: Otoboke Beaver - Itekoma Hits
excerpt: Otoboke Beaver didn’t need to go this hard!

title: Lil Nas X - 7
excerpt: On 7, Lil Nas X shows some admirable versatility while leaving plenty of room for growth.

title: Waste of Space Orchestra - Syntheosis
excerpt: Waste of Space Orchestra delivers an immaculately produced fusion of doom metal, psych and space rock, but the performances and compositions can be lackluster.

title: Prince - Originals
excerpt: The demos that comprise Originals blow most artists’ finished studio work out of the water.

title: black midi - Schlagenheim
excerpt: Right out of the gate, black midi has crafted one of the decade’s most creative rock albums.

title: Blarf - Cease & Desist
excerpt: Comedian and actor Eric André’s very own musical side-project serves up a wild, sample-based ride into the demented side of plunderphonics on Cease & Desist. Not only that, but this record also serves as a giant middle finger to the limitations modern copyright law places on artistic expression within the auditory realm. Equal parts absurd and revolutionary: This is Blarf.

title: Jaden - ERYS
excerpt: I think Jaden heard Astroworld.

title: Chance the Rapper - The Big Day
excerpt: More like The Big Mess.

title: Benny the Butcher - The Plugs I Met
excerpt: Benny is no doubt a capable rapper and lyricist, but he tends to be overshadowed by the guests on this new EP.

title: Oh Sees - Face Stabber
excerpt: Face Stabber is perhaps Oh Sees’ most ambitious album to date, but its protracted jams wear out their welcome before long.

title: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard - Infest the Rats' Nest
excerpt: King Gizzard takes a successful swing at thrash metal on their second album of 2019.

title: Trippie Redd - !
excerpt: To say the least, ! does not follow through on the potential of Trippie Redd’s previous work.

title: Knocked Loose - A Different Shade of Blue
excerpt: Breakdowns galore on Knocked Loose’s death metal-infused sophomore album, though it’s sometimes hard to tell one from the next.

title: BROCKHAMPTON - GINGER
excerpt: GINGER is a return to form for the BROCKHAMPTON boys, albeit a decidedly downcast one.

title: Lana Del Rey - Norman Fucking Rockwell!
excerpt: Lana Del Rey improves as a songwriter by leaps and bounds on NFR.

title: EarthGang - Mirrorland
excerpt: EarthGang’s shortcomings become apparent when they tone the intensity down midway through Mirrorland.

title: Post Malone - Hollywood's Bleeding
excerpt: Post Malone loses focus on his sophomore album.

title: JPEGMAFIA - All My Heroes Are Cornballs
excerpt: I’m not disappointed. That’s for sure.

title: Travis Scott - "Highest in the Room"
Ana Frango Elétrico - Little Electric Chicken Heart
excerpt: Ana Frango Elétrico’s authentically vintage fusion of chamber pop, rock, samba, and jazz is a real blast!

title: Danny Brown - uknowhatimsayin¿
excerpt: For the most part, uknowhatimsayin¿ is an amusingly subversive update on some classic rap formulas.

title: Ariel Pink - Odditties Sodomies Vol. 2
excerpt: A quick review of the new Ariel Pink compilation—it’s good!

title: Lil Peep - Everybody's Everything
excerpt: Everybody’s Everything, while a mixed bag, isn’t the tasteless cash grab that posthumous releases these days tend to be.

title: Westside Gunn - Hitler Wears Hermes 7
excerpt: Westside Gunn’s grimy vibe remains the best thing going for him, while songwriting remains his Achilles heel.

title: Swans - leaving meaning.
excerpt: Leaving Meaning, while frequently stunning, feels more like a reiteration for Swans than it does an evolution.

title: Trippie Redd - A Love Letter to You 4
excerpt: A handful of highlights aside, A Love Letter to You 4′s shelf life isn’t much longer than its runtime.

title: Liturgy - H.A.Q.Q.
excerpt: H.A.Q.Q. is the culmination of all of Ravenna Hunt-Hendrix’s musical innovations this decade.

title: Kanye West - My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
excerpt: In celebration of hitting 2 million subscribers, I’m finally answering the requests to do a re-review of Kanye West’s most celebrated album, My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy.

title: Lim Kim - Generasian
excerpt: Generasian is a promising start to this adventurous new chapter of Lim Kim’s career.

title: Makaya McCraven - We're New Again
excerpt: While often pretty and groovy, Makaya McCraven’s reimagining of Gil Scott-Heron’s swansong tends to drain the suspense and emotional potency out of its source material.

title: Squarepusher - Be Up a Hello
excerpt: While not as cohesive as Squarepusher’s seminal works, Be Up a Hello is his most solid work in at least a decade.

title: Bladee - EXETER
excerpt: Bladee’s shoddy vocals stifle the imaginative EXETER.

title: Sufjan Stevens & Lowell Brams - Aporia
excerpt: Sufjan Stevens teams up with stepfather Lowell Brams for a severely underwhelming series of half-hearted ambient works.

title: Westside Gunn - Pray for Paris
excerpt: Pray for Paris does Westside Gunn’s established style well for the most part, but isn’t likely to convert many nonbelievers.

title: Rina Sawayama - Sawayama
excerpt: Rina Sawayama comes to us as a near-fully formed popstar on her debut album.

title: Nav - Good Intentions / Brown Boy 2
excerpt: Nav more than earns his NOT GOOD hat-trick with this new double album.

title: Elder - Omens
excerpt: Elder goes full prog with mixed results on Omens.

title: KSI - Dissimulation
excerpt: While KSI surpasses most of his YouTube peers-gone-rappers, he doesn’t yet stand out in the current hip hop landscape.

title: Yung Lean - Starz
excerpt: The songwriting and vocal performances on Starz often leave a lot to be desired, though the Whitearmor production is pretty stellar.

title: Ka - Descendants of Cain
excerpt: While Descendants of Cain doesn’t have the consistent mythos of Orpheus vs. the Sirens and is at times typical for Ka, his pen game and delivery are as sharp as ever.

title: Freddie Gibbs & The Alchemist - Alfredo
excerpt: The Alchemist’s versatile production soundtracks some of Gangsta Gibbs’ best flows and performances yet on Alfredo.

title: Backxwash - God Has Nothing to Do With This Leave Him Out of It
excerpt: With its chilling mix of rap, goth, punk, and noise, God Has Nothing to Do With This has a huge impact for such a concise project.

title: Chloe x Halle - Ungodly Hour
excerpt: On their sophomore album, Chloe and Halle take a versatile and tasteful approach to contemporary R&B.

title: Armand Hammer - Shrines
excerpt: Though Shrines is Armand Hammer’s least direct effort thus far, Billy Woods and Elucid continue to have one of the most compelling dynamics in modern hip hop.

title: Juice WRLD - Legends Never Die
excerpt: Legends Never Die effectively honors Juice WRLD’s style and legacy.

title: Hum - Inlet
excerpt: Returning after decades of studio album silence, Hum tries to reintroduce their classic sound with some added bells and whistles, but falls quite short.

title: Arca - KiCk i
excerpt: KiCk i is a promising kick-off to this exciting new chapter of Arca’s life and career.

title: Logic - No Pressure
excerpt: Better late than never, Logic is back to being a rapper worth rooting for on No Pressure.

title: Paysage d'Hiver - Im Wald
excerpt: Im Wald stretches Paysage d’Hiver’s most threadbare material to an arduous two hours.

title: Big Sean - Detroit 2
excerpt: Detroit 2 is far and away Big Sean’s best album.

title: 6ix9ine - TattleTales
excerpt: Listening to TattleTales is like volunteering to be trolled, and it may not even succeed on that front.

title: Bladee - 333
excerpt: 333‘s ethereality may be roughly executed, but Bladee is onto something with this increasingly blissful direction.

title: Spillage Village - Spilligion
excerpt: There is undeniably a lot of talent between the members of Spillage Village, but it often doesn’t manifest as memorable songwriting or topical focus on Spilligion.

title: Slauson Malone - Vergangenheitsbewältigung
excerpt: This spiritual successor to A Quiet Farwell flexes Slauson Malone’s singer-songwriter muscle.

title: Nav - Emergency Tsunami
excerpt: 2020 needed a third NAV album.

title: Gorillaz - Song Machine, Season One: Strange Timez
excerpt: Gorillaz compiles a bunch of damn good singles to make a damn good album.

title: 21 Savage & Metro Boomin - Savage Mode II
excerpt: Savage Mode II is a rare instance of the sequel being WAY better than the original.

title: Bad Bunny - El Último Tour del Mundo
excerpt: Bad Bunny’s third album of 2020 is a bit of a rough ride.

title: Megan Thee Stallion - Good News
excerpt: Megan Thee Stallion sells herself short artistically on her still mostly decent debut album.

title: Ichiko Aoba - Windswept Adan
excerpt: Stunningly serene.

title: lobsterfight - pink, black, and orange in the corners.
excerpt: lobsterfight’s rough-and-ready debut is one of the year’s most promising indie and emo showings.

title: The Avalanches - We Will Always Love You
excerpt: For as stylistically cohesive and seamlessly flowing as We Will Always Love You is, it’s somehow a tale of two albums.

title: Kid Cudi - Man on the Moon III: The Chosen
excerpt: The Chosen is Kid Cudi’s best solo project since the second Man on the Moon (and it may even have that one beat).

title: Viagra Boys - Welfare Jazz
excerpt: On their sophomore album, Viagra Boys tell a love story via punk eclecticism.

title: Nine Inch Nails - The Downward Spiral
excerpt: It’s a testament to Trent Reznor’s songwriting skills that his sophomore album, an abrasive and harrowing concept album about self-destruction, became a multi-platinum hit.

title: The Roots - Things Fall Apart
excerpt: Classics Week 2021 kicks off with Things Fall Apart, the 1999 breakthrough in The Roots’ increasingly ambitious career, and a milestone for hip hop at large.

title: Hayley Williams - FLOWERS for VASES / descansos
excerpt: Hayley Williams has transposed the derivativeness of her debut album to an indie folk context.

title: R.A.P. Ferreira - bob's son
excerpt: While not one of Ferreira’s most robust releases, bob’s son is peppered with interesting and enjoyable ideas.

title: Ad Nauseam - Imperative Imperceptible Impulse
excerpt: Ad Nauseam bring fiery performances, dynamic production, and revelatory fusions of metal, classical music, and jazz on their sophomore album.

title: Black Dresses - Forever in Your Heart
excerpt: Black Dresses go harder than ever before on their first post-disbandment album.

title: Nick Cave & Warren Ellis - Carnage
excerpt: The emotionally potent and timely Carnage finds Nick Cave and Warren Ellis letting loose with the aesthetic they forged on the previous Bad Seeds trilogy.

title: Conway & Big Ghost Ltd - If It Bleeds It Can Be Killed
excerpt: Conway and Big Ghost display a creative chemistry that hopefully continues into the future.

title: Denzel Curry x Kenny Beats - Unlocked 1.5
excerpt: Unlocked‘s remixes are kind of hit-and-miss, but should be worth checking out for anyone who enjoyed the original project.

title: Architects - For Those That Wish to Exist
excerpt: An over-orchestrated earsore.

title: NF - Clouds
excerpt: NF might be a tad overhated.

title: C. Tangana - El Madrileño
excerpt: El Madrileño is hopefully the beginning of an exciting new trajectory for C. Tangana.

title: Young Stoner Life, Young Thug, Gunna - Slime Language 2
excerpt: Young Thug and company are back with an even more bloated and inconsistent comp-like album.

title: Iglooghost - Lei Line Eon
excerpt: At its best, Lei Line Eon‘s new direction exposes the nuances and beauty of Iglooghost’s production, but it’s not without its incongruities and growing pains.

title: Armand Hammer & The Alchemist - Haram
excerpt: The Alchemist helps Armand Hammer make their most surreal album yet.

title: DJ Khaled - Khaled Khaled
excerpt: When you inevitably hear Khaled Khaled at the barbershop or blaring from a passing car, some of it won’t be so bad.

title: Porter Robinson - Nurture
excerpt: Spellbinding.

title: Panopticon - ...And Again Into the Light
excerpt: …And Again Into the Light is a stunning re-consolidation of Austin Lunn’s sound.

title: Weezer - Van Weezer
excerpt: Between a few tracks hitting and Rivers singing “pump it up into me, please daddy” as a hook, Van Weezer is pretty much a mid-tier Weezer album.

title: Sweet Trip - A Tiny House, In Secret Speeches, Polar Equals
excerpt: Sweet Trip is mostly unaffected by the comeback curse on A Tiny House.

title: Tyler, the Creator - Call Me If You Get Lost
excerpt: This is how to flex.

title: Gaspard Augé - Escapades
excerpt: Escapades fails to exemplify what made its classic and progressive electronic inspirations so wonderful.

title: IDK - USEE4YOURSELF
excerpt: You have to trudge through a lot of middling pop rap to reach USEE4YOURSELF‘s pockets of emotional potency.

title: Clairo - Sling
excerpt: Clairo displays considerable growth as a songwriter since Immunity on Sling.

title: ZelooperZ - Van Gogh's Left Ear
excerpt: Van Gogh’s Left Ear gets off to a very strong start before ZelooperZ’s risk-taking leads to some awkward spots.

title: $uicideboy$ - Long Term Effects of SUFFERING
excerpt: For better or worse, $uicideboy$ stick to their guns on Long Term Effects.

title: Nas - King's Disease II
excerpt: King’s Disease II capitalizes on all the potential of its predecessor.

title: The Killers - Pressure Machine
excerpt: Having flirted with heartland rock on their previous album, The Killers delve much deeper into the sound on the conceptual Pressure Machine.

title: Deafheaven - Infinite Granite
excerpt: Infinite Granite finds Deafheaven eschewing the blackened aspect of their sound in favor of boilerplate shoegaze and post-rock.

title: Sault - Nine
excerpt: While Nine pales in comparison to the collective’s 2020 output, it’s still well worth checking out…while you still can.

title: Injury Reserve - By the Time I Get to Phoenix
excerpt: Injury Reserve pulled something of a masterpiece from a truly hellish year.

title: Drake - Certified Lover Boy
excerpt: Certified snoozer.

title: Magdalena Bay - Mercurial World
excerpt: Even while the duo’s finding a distinct sound, Mercurial World serves bop after bop.

title: illuminati hotties - Let Me Do One More
excerpt: The one we’ve been waiting for.

title: Tropical Fuck Storm - Deep States
excerpt: Deep States is TFS’s weakest batch of songs yet, which is to say it’s not that bad.

title: James Blake - Friends That Break Your Heart
excerpt: James’ best record since his debut.

title: The War on Drugs - I Don't Live Here Anymore
excerpt: The War on Drugs’ heartland rock sound is more direct than ever on I Don’t Live Here Anymore, with Granduciel’s vocals and writing not always up to the task.

title: Mastodon - Hushed and Grim
excerpt: While a lot more impressive than the preceding Emperor of Sand, Hushed and Grim does buckle under its own weight.

title: JPEGMAFIA - LP!
excerpt: And still undefeated: JPEGMAFIA!

title: Limp Bizkit - Still Sucks
excerpt: Ah shit, here we go again.

title: Marissa Nadler - The Path of the Clouds
excerpt: The Path of the Clouds is easily Marissa Nadler’s most instrumentally dense solo project to date, which is mostly a blessing.

title: Idles - Crawler
excerpt: Crawler lacks the impact of the band’s past few LPs.

title: Sloppy Jane - Madison
excerpt: Madison is one of the year’s most beautiful and enigmatic records.

title: Gunna - DS4EVER
excerpt: DS4EVER offers little to nothing between its vocal performances, songwriting, and production.

title: Aesop Rock x Blockhead - Garbology
excerpt: Garbology should be a treat for fans of this pair’s seminal work together.

title: FKA twigs - Caprisongs
excerpt: Caprisongs is twigs’ catchiest and most fun project to date.

title: Roddy Ricch - Live Life Fast
excerpt: LLF follows up on none of the potential of Roddy’s debut.

title: Silvana Estrada - Marchita
excerpt: What Marchita has in concision it also has in beauty and emotional potency.

title: Cordae - From a Birds Eye View

excerpt: Art Pop is easily Lady Gaga’s most eccentric and colorfully produced album yet. However, she still doesn’t go far enough to keep her very radio-friendly band of pop interesting for an entire album–especially when it comes to lyrics.

title: Action Bronson & Party Supplies - Blue Chips 2
excerpt: While East Coast MC Action Bronson didn’t skimp on the personality with this new tape of his, there are certainly a lot of aimless, short-of-breath tracks here that really feel like filler.

title: Isaiah Rashad - Cilvia Demo
excerpt: While Tennessee rapper Isaiah Rashad proves himself as a capable spitter and lyricist on this project, it’s the storytelling, instrumentals, and choruses that are occasionally lackluster.

title: Murmur - Self-Titled
excerpt: Murmur’s self-titled sophomore album is a impressively executed fusion of black metal and progressive rock.

title: The War On Drugs - Lost In the Dream
excerpt: The new War On Drugs album is a winning combination of psychedelic rock, krautrock, folk, and Americana–just like the band’s last album, but better.

title: Migos - No Label II
excerpt: When it comes to loud, visceral trap rap, there are plenty of songs worth recommending on this new Migos mixtape. The problem is it’s so packed with filler that finding the cartoony, eccentric, and occasionally hilarious gems on this thing can be a bit of a chore.

title: CunninLynguists - Strange Journey Vol. 3
excerpt: CunninLynguists pack their latest project with one track after another of quality features.

title: Avey Tare's Slasher Flicks - Enter The Slasher House
excerpt: While this new Avey Tare record has some sweet melodies on it, nearly every piece of instrumentation on this thing is burnt to a crisp with effects. A lot like the latest Animal Collective record, this album is a little overdone, and could have benefited from taking the more orthodox approach the “Little Fang” single did.

title: Pixies - Indie Cindy
excerpt: Pixies return with a textbook example of a disappointing comeback record.

title: Twin Shadow - "To The Top"
excerpt: The new single from George Lewis Jr., a.k.a. Twin Shadow, is pure power ballad mimicry. You might dig it if, you know, you’re into that sorta thing.

title: The Black Keys - Turn Blue
excerpt: The Black Keys drop their most bloated and tame album to date with Turn Blue.

title: Jenny Lewis - The Voyager
excerpt: Famed songstress Jenny Lewis drops her most commercial effort yet with The Voyager.

title: "Weird Al" Yankovic - Mandatory Fun
excerpt: “Weird Al” is back and sounding funnier than ever on his most timely and sharp album in years.

title: Travi$ Scott - Days Before Rodeo
excerpt: TX rapper, producer, and songwriter Travi$ Scott delivers a mixtape that’s only marginally better than his previous effort, Owl Pharaoh.

title: Michael Cera - True That
excerpt: Michael Cera drops an album that’s a musical hobbyist’s affair.

title: Busdriver - Perfect Hair
excerpt: Art rap vet Busdriver drops one of his most exciting and confounding albums yet.

title: Death From Above 1979 - The Physical World

title: The Game - The Documentary 2

title: Panda Bear - Mr. Noah

title: DJ Shadow - Endtroducing.....

title: SOPHIE - Product

title: M.E.D. Blu and Madlib - Bad Neighbor

title: Denzel Curry - Imperial

title: Drake - Views

title: Clams Casino - 32 Levels

title: Crystal Castles - Amnesty (I)

title: 2 8 1 4 - Rain Temple
excerpt: 2 8 1 4 returns with a followup to the duo’s infamous 新しい日の誕生 album.

title: M.I.A. - AIM
excerpt: ZZZZZZzzZzzzZZZzzZZzzZzZZZZ

title: Isaiah Rashad - The Sun's Tirade

title: Mac Miller - The Divine Feminine

title: Migos - Culture

title: Rick Ross - Rather You Than Me

title: Grouper - The Man Who Died In His Boat
excerpt:

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Crystal Castles- III

WATCH THE REVIEW

title: Arcade Fire - Reflektor
excerpt: I’ve been on the fence about many albums this year, but this is one of the few where I’m torn. Rather than deliver another cohesive set of songs, Reflektor embarks upon a stylistic hodgepodge full of hits and misses.

title: Danger Mouse & Daniele Luppi- "The Rose With the Broken Neck"
excerpt:
On “the Rose With the Broken Neck,” Danger Mouse & Daniele Luppi pull together some Italian-style soundtrack music with Jack White on vocals. Though the textures and sounds are vintage and pretty authentic, the drama of this track–the drama I imagine should be here–doesn’t really hit me. The same goes for the other tracks as well.

The level of romance and passion on the music that influences this album is sky-high, but this feels more like a barren wasteland of pretended-ed-ed emotions.

title: Cynic - "Humanoid"
excerpt:
Cynic has returned with “Humanoid,” their first piece of new music since 2014’s Kindly Bent to Free Us. Moreover, the song strikes me as a return to form following that album’s disappointing mildness. The band’s back to creating sharp, inventive prog-metal – and holy shit are those basslines mind-blowing!


The single didn’t coincide with an album announcement, but a new one this year through Season of Mist certainly appears to be in the cards.

title: Carnage & Lil Pump - "i Shyne"
excerpt:
DJ Carnage recently linked up with everyone’s favorite DAMN. analog, Lil Pump; and the result is just raw, explosive energy in the form of “i Shyne.” Our boy Lil Pump SNAPS on this track, matching the crazy wailing sample / synth line that propels Carnage’s beat. This song apparently came together pretty quickly and effortlessly, so hopefully this won’t be the only time these two team up.

Young Fathers have just announced the release of their third album, Cocoa Sugar, through Ninja Tune later this year. Yes, the Edinburgh trio is back, and I’m just stunned thinking about the artistic progression the trio has undergone to get to the point they’re at with this new track, “In My View.” It was only five years ago when I was praising Tape One and Two, a pair of creative lo-fi hip hop EPs with splashes of soul and West African music thrown in..

title: Mount Eerie - "Distortion"
excerpt:
Mount Eerie has shared the lengthy lead single from his forthcoming album, Now Only. “Distortion” lives up to its title right out of the gate and suggests that this will perhaps be the Ocean Roar to A Crow Looked at Me‘s Clear Moon. The songwriting is also sounding more Kozelek-inspired than ever, down to the details about a one-night stand Phil had many years ago. Exciting to hear him further develop this candid approach to lyricism.


Now Only drops March 16 via P.W. Elverum & Sun.

As you may have already noticed from the title, much of what the band does is slug-themed (I think it’s specifically giant space slugs, but don’t quote me on that). excerpt: This past week, eminent metalcore outfit Converge released their ninth album, The Dusk in Us. Above you can check out a poetic, though visually overwhelming video for the opening track, “A Single Tear” – a loud, anguished, and multi-phased meditation on parenthood. Seems we’re picking up where the band’s emotional high-water mark, All We Love We Leave Behind, left off.

The track is one of many bonuses on the super deluxe version of Humanz, which is out now. Well, this would’ve been a highlight.

title: Ought - "These 3 Things"

It’ll be the band’s Merge Records debut and will follow up their great 2015 album, Sun Coming Down – just listen to it already!

And they’re apparently making good on their promise of five albums this year, so I guess we’ll be hearing this one real soon.

title: SOPHIE - "It's Okay to Cry"

Cautiously optimistic about a WESTSIDEDOOM album.

Injury Reserve has announced an EP titled Drive It Like It’s Stolen that’s due out at the end of the month. Drive It Like It’s Stolen on September 29.

title: Wu-Tang Clan - "People Say" ft. Redman
excerpt: RZA has announced that the first release on his newly-founded 36 Chambers ALC will be a 10-track Wu-Tang album titled The Saga Continues. It’s great to hear Redman back in the fold with the group on this lead single, which also features a solid set of verses from Method Man and Raekwon. The saga continues October 13.

title: Mogwai - "Eternal Panther"
excerpt: The latest B-side from Mogwai’s new album Every Country’s Sun finds the Glaswegian post-rockers taking a refreshing turn toward more direct songwriting. “Eternal Panther” is a short, sweet, and to the point noise rock tune in the vein of Dinosaur Jr. (I’m far from the first person to make that comparison, but it’s very apt). Being a non-album track, it isn’t really indicative of the band’s current direction, but at any rate, Every Country’s Sun drops September 1 via Temporary Residence.

title: Wolves in the Throne Room - "Angrboda"
excerpt: Atmospheric black metal outfit Wolves in the Throne Room has released the epic centerpiece of its upcoming album, Thrice Woven. A slightly truncated version of “Angrboda” was premiered earlier last week by Adult Swim to coincide with the solar eclipse, but now here it is in all its glory. Thrice Woven is out September 22 via the band’s Artemisia imprint.

excerpt: Primus harkens back to their Frizzle Fry days with the toned-down yet musically inventive title track from their upcoming album, The Desaturating Seven. excerpt: Iglooghost continues to be one of the most imaginative electronic music producers in the game with “Bug Thief,” probably the closest aural analog to watching an episode of Adventure Time there’s ever been. The track is off Neō Wax Bloom, the full-length Brainfeeder debut I’ve been waiting to hear from him for years – finally dropping September 29.

title: Benjamin Clementine - "God Save the Jungle"
excerpt: I missed Benjamin Clementine’s latest single while on vacation, but good thing I went back for it because this is some of the London singer-songwriter’s most potent, visceral work yet. “God Save the Jungle” isn’t at all la-di-da like some of the stuff on Benjamin’s (still quite good) 2015 debut At Least for Now. Looking forward to what his sophomore effort, I Tell a Fly, brings next month.

title: Brockhampton - "Gummy"
excerpt: With its stellar flows from Kevin Abstract and a G-funk vibe coming through in its instrumental, “Gummy” has my mouth watering even more for Saturation II, which is thankfully slated to drop later this month!

title: TWIABP - "Dillon and Her Son"
excerpt: The World Is a Beautiful Place has announced their third album, titled Always Foreign, and with that has come a somewhat divisive lead single. The sound the band goes for here is closer to pop punk than Midwest emo, but I can appreciate it as one of the catchiest songs the band has written to date. Always Foreign drops September 29 via Epitaph.

title: Liars - "Coins in My Caged Fist" / "The Grand Delusional"
excerpt: Liars have released two more singles from their upcoming album Theme from Crying Fountain – “Coins in My Caged Fist” continues down the rabbit hole of uncanny electronica, while “The Grand Delusional” is a predominantly acoustic affair. TFCF is out August 25 via Mute.

title: 10 Worst Songs of My Adolescence Pt. 1
excerpt:
A few years back, I made a handful of guest videos for a channel that has since been rebranded and unlisted its older content. I’ve got permission to re-upload the vids, so for now here’s the most requested one. You guys just really want to see me relive horrible musical memories from my youth. Or maybe it’s all about that haircut.


Originally posted March 19, 2014.

title: Chelsea Wolfe - "Vex"
excerpt: Here’s the second single from Chelsea Wolfe’s heavy new album Hiss Spun. “Vex” has pretty much all the qualities I liked about “16 Psyche,” but I especially love the grim, growled vocals lent by Aaron Turner this time. Hiss Spun is out September 22 through Sargent House.

title: Converge - "I Can Tell You About Pain" / "Eve"
excerpt: Converge is back with their first pieces of new music in five years! Admittedly, the lead single “I Can Tell You About Pain” kind of strikes me as the band by the numbers, but the B-side “Eve” is fucking epic and effectively expands upon some of the slow and sludgy ideas from All We Love We Leave Behind. Check em out above and below.

title: The Killers - "Run for Cover"
excerpt: The Killers have a new album on the way titled Wonderful Wonderful, and this latest single is a peppy piece of post-punk revivalism that I’m pleasantly surprised to say lives up to that title. The album drops September 22 via Island.

title: Susanne Sundfør - "Mountaineers" ft. John Grant
excerpt: Susanne Sundfør teams up with former Czars frontman John Grant on “Mountaineers,” probably her spaciest track to date – with an amazing ending to boot. It’s the second single from the Norwegian singer-songwriter’s upcoming album Music for People in Trouble, which will be released August 25 via Bella Union.

title: Wolf Parade - "Valley Boy"
excerpt: This new Wolf Parade single brings back the visceral rock instrumentation and dramatic lead vocals that made the band exciting in the first place. Cry Cry Cry, their first album in seven years, drops October 6 via Sub Pop.

title: Grizzly Bear - "Neighbors"
excerpt: Of all the singles to have come out in promotion of Grizzly Bear’s new album Painted Ruins, this latest one strikes me as being the most powerful in terms of composition and instrumentation. You can give it a listen above, along with its video, which offers quite a surreal vision of nature and domesticity. The album is out August 18 via RCA.

title: Uncommon Nasa - "Written at Night" ft. Billy Woods & Quelle Chris
excerpt:
Written at Night by Uncommon Nasa



Staten Island MC Uncommon Nasa is dropping his first entirely self-produced album next month on Man Bites Dog Records. It’s called Written at Night, and the tracklist looks almost like a who’s who of current underground hip hop, featuring Open Mike Eagle, Billy Woods, Quelle Chris, and many more. Stream the title/closing track, which features two of those names, up there.

title: Deerhoof - "Your Dystopic Creation Doesn't Fear You" ft. Awkwafina
excerpt:
Deerhoof makes its mark on the Adult Swim Singles Program with “Your Dystopic Creation Doesn’t Fear You.” Probably one of the wordier titles in the series, and it features a gritty opening verse from “My Vag” rapper Awkwafina, who fits the band’s angular riffing remarkably well.


The track appears on the band’s upcoming album Mountain Moves, which features many more collaborations – Lætitia Sadier, Xenia Rubinos, and Matana Roberts just to name a few. It’s out September 8 via Joyful Noise.

title: Is Hip Hop More Popular Than Rock? (DEHH Guest Video)
excerpt: Has rap music replaced rock in the cultural zeitgeist? Hip hop is everywhere and it doesn’t seem to be slowing down in terms of popularity and influence. A polarizing genre known for it’s controversial figures, it’s hard to deny the impact hip hop has had in the cultures of the world. How has this happened? Will it continue? title: STINKPIECE: The Media Obsession w/ Tyler, The Creator's Sexuality
excerpt: In the wake of Tyler, the Creator’s new album Scum Fuck Flower Boy prematurely finding its way onto the Internet, several popular music/culture websites have seen it fit not only to publicize the leak, but to give early evaluations of the album’s revelations about Tyler’s sexuality. Today I’m reacting to one of MANY pieces published by Highsnobiety, probably the worst offender in this situation.

title: DJ Shadow - "Horror Show" ft. Danny Brown
excerpt:
For a track on his new EP The Mountain Has Fallen, DJ Shadow teamed up with Danny Brown and the results are fucking fireworks! The producer and rapper complement each other perfectly as they deliver a tour de force of grimy hip hop that’s well off the beaten path.


The EP, which also features Nas and Academy Award-winning composer Steven Price, is out now via Mass Appeal.

title: Zombie Juice - "Lava"
excerpt: Zombie Juice of Flatbush Zombies goes solo (sort of) here on this new single “Lava.” The instrumental isn’t the hardest banger Erick has ever produced, but Juice’s energetic flow and unique voice carries the track and keeps me on the edge of my seat. I don’t know if he or the Zombies are gearing up for an album, but this sure sounds promising.

title: Best & Worst Tracks: 7/9 (Blue Ivy Carter, Kesha, DJ Shadow, Ringo Starr, Kamaiyah, Coldplay)
excerpt: The weekly segment in which Anthony touches down on some of the best and worst tracks he has heard in the past week.

title: milo - "magician (suture)"
excerpt:
who told you to think??!!?!?!?! by milo



Everything that impressed me about milo‘s previous album, including Kenny Segal’s intricate production, is in full force on this latest single “magician (suture).” The stuttering vocal edits in particular might be the coolest production trick I’ve heard on one of milo’s projects yet. His new album, who told you to think??!!?!?!?!, drops August 11 via Ruby Yacht.

title: Olga Bell - "Special Leave"
excerpt: Glitchy singer-songwriter Olga Bell has a new EP out called America, which takes its name from and includes three different mixes of the closing track from her 2016 album Tempo. But the highlight of the set is the non-album cut “Special Leave,” which features one of Olga’s most stunning vocal performances and a complex, polyrhythmic dance beat.

title: Jeremy's Mid-Year Faves 2017
excerpt:
Hello good folks, Jeremy here, lead video editor for The Needle Drop. It’s one of those times again when Anthony’s underlings step out of his melonheaded shadow for a brief moment of sunshine. This time it’s for a mid-year list. Basically, here are fifteen albums from the first half of the year that I enjoyed the most and am still listening to – including while they play on repeat in my head – as June comes to a close.


I want to point out that this is an alphabetical list.

title: 10 Times I Changed My Opinion on Albums
excerpt: Opinions change! Get used to it! Here’s me talking about 10 albums that my perception has altered on to some degree. Love ya!

title: Best & Worst Tracks: 6/18 (DJ Khaled, Bones, Chelsea Wolfe, Arcade Fire, Dizzee Rascal)
excerpt: The weekly segment in which Anthony touches down on some of the best and worst tracks he has heard in the past week.

title: Queens of the Stone Age - "The Way You Used to Do"
excerpt: Queens of the Stone Age’s previous album, …Like Clockwork, was one of the best rock albums the year it came out, and arguably the band’s most downbeat and sobering release to date. But things are slated to take a poppy turn with the Mark Ronson-produced Villains, coming out August 25. I think he and QOTSA jell pretty well on this lead single, but you be the judge.

title: Chelsea Wolfe - "16 Psyche"
excerpt: In 2015, Chelsea Wolfe released her heaviest record to date, Abyss, and judging from “16 Psyche” here, it seems things are only going to get heavier and darker on her next record, Hiss Spun. A doom metal album recorded by Chelsea Wolfe and Kurt Ballou? That’s a wet nightmare come true! Hiss Spun will drop September 22 via Sargent House.

title: Washed Out - "Hard to Say Goodbye"
excerpt: Chillwave spearhead Washed Out ventures in a digable nu-disco direction on new single “Hard to Say Goodbye.” It’s taken from his upcoming visual album Mister Mellow, out June 30 via Stones Throw.

title: Bones - "SeanPaulWasNeverThereToGimmeTheLight" ft. Danny Brown
excerpt: Bones comes through with a brilliantly-titled dark banger featuring a verse from none other than Danny Brown! The track is featured on Bones’ new NoRedeemingQualities mixtape.

excerpt: The weekly segment in which Anthony touches down on some of the best and worst tracks he has heard in the past week.

title: STINKPIECE: The Beatles Are for Men!!!
excerpt: Today I’m responding to a wonderful thinkpiece Salon published to commemorate the 50th anniversary of The Beatles’ Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band, which claims that the seminal album forever ruined rock music for women. Brace yourselves, this might just be the foulest stinker yet.
